title: Canadian publisher drops Thélyson Orélien after confirming AI use in debut novel
content: A Canadian publisher announced on Wednesday that it has dropped Thélyson Orélien, a prize-nominated writer. The decision follows new information confirming that Orélien used artificial intelligence to write his acclaimed debut novel.
summary: A Canadian publisher dropped prize-nominated writer Thélyson Orélien on Wednesday. This decision followed new information indicating he used artificial intelligence to write his acclaimed debut novel.
author: France 24

title: Trump faces new scrutiny over ties to Putin labeled “humanitarian”
content:
US President Donald Trump’s shift in focus away from Ukraine has raised new questions regarding his relationship with Russian leader Vladimir Putin. A top American envoy described Putin as a "humanitarian" on Wednesday, highlighting the complex nature of the US-Russia dynamic.

Trump has framed his interactions with Putin as part of a comprehensive agreement that resulted in the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard. According to Trump, this deal is also intended to conclude Russia’s war on Ukraine.
summary: US President Donald Trump’s shift away from Ukraine has sparked fresh questions about his attachment to Russian leader Vladimir Putin, whom a top American envoy called a “humanitarian.” Trump says his dealings with Putin are part of a mega‑deal that secured the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard and will end Russia’s war on Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Le Pen to launch campaign as polls show wide first-round lead
content:
Marine Le Pen will officially launch her presidential campaign this weekend at a two‑day National Rally congress in Orléans.  

The latest Ifop poll, conducted after mass protests and riots in France, indicates that Le Pen would win the first round of the presidential election by a wide margin.  

The poll also shows far‑left candidate Jean‑Luc Melenchon as the most likely opponent in a potential runoff.  FRANCE 24’s Emerald Maxwell reports.
summary: Marine Le Pen will officially launch her presidential campaign at the National Rally congress in Orléans this weekend. A recent Ifop poll indicates she would win the first round by a wide margin, with Jean-Luc Melenchon as her likely opponent in the runoff.
author: France 24

title: Sudanese Army Drone Strike on Abyei Market Kills 153
content:
The death toll from a drone strike on the Amiet market in Abyei district, an area disputed between Sudan and South Sudan, has risen to 153, with local authorities indicating the figure is likely higher. A local official told AFP on Wednesday that the strike, which occurred on Monday, involved multiple munitions and was carried out by the Sudanese army.

In a discussion with FRANCE 24’s Mark Owen, Jan Pospisil, a Sudan Affairs Analyst at the Peace and Conflict Resolution Evidence Platform, commented on the incident. Pospisil noted that the Sudanese army has long attempted to portray itself as humane on the international stage while characterizing the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as committing atrocities. He stated that the recent attack clearly demonstrates that there is not much difference between the two groups, adding that neither the Sudanese military nor the RSF shows any acknowledgement of human life in the conflict.
summary: A drone strike on the Amiet market in Abyei district killed 153 people, authorities say. The strike, carried out by the Sudanese army using multiple munitions, was reported by a local official to AFP and the death toll is likely higher.
author: France 24

title: Trump uses France riots to push false immigration claims before midterms
content: Donald Trump and his inner circle are utilizing unrest in France to promote unsubstantiated claims that attribute the riots to immigration, a strategy that includes displaying French protest footage at midterm rallies. Despite the lack of evidence linking immigration to the disturbances, French President Emmanuel Macron has accused world leaders of making “stupid comments” at France’s expense. This political maneuvering occurs as Republicans face increasing pressure ahead of the midterms, coinciding with Trump’s approval rating reaching a reported record low.
summary: Trump uses France riots to push false immigration claims before midterms.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine supports US proposal for urgent three‑way talks with Russia and the United States
content:
President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Wednesday that Ukraine supports a U.S. proposal for three‑way talks with Russia and the United States at the level of negotiators. He added that the talks should take place as soon as possible, preferably no later than early November.  

In an interview with FRANCE 24, Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe, Russia and Eurasia Programme at Chatham House, noted that it is unclear whether Russian President Vladimir Putin would meet U.S. President Donald Trump and President Zelenskiy. Roos added that meeting Zelenskiy is the last thing Putin would be prepared to do.
summary: Ukraine supports US proposal for urgent three‑way talks with Russia and the United States.
author: France 24

title: Raids at far‑right group’s European Parliament offices amid funding inquiry
content: Authorities searched the Patriots’ European Parliament offices as part of a long‑running funding inquiry. The group says the charges relate to its predecessor and that there is no legal continuity between the two.
summary: Authorities searched the Patriots' European Parliament offices as part of a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges relate to its predecessor and that there is no legal continuity between the two.
author: DW World

title: Moscow pushes summit with Trump and Xi to end Ukraine war, excluding Kyiv and EU
content: Moscow is pushing for a summit that would bring former U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping together to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The proposed meeting would exclude Kyiv and the European Union. Details of what Russia hopes to achieve or why China might agree remain unspecified.
summary: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The proposed meeting would exclude Kyiv and the EU.
author: DW World

title: Sudan peace talks continue in Geneva to halt fighting and ease humanitarian crisis
content: Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.
summary: Talks to halt fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis continued in Geneva on Wednesday. Nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.
author: UN News

title: UN agencies appeal for help to protect weakest from unprecedented El Niño
content: Two UN agencies issued a powerful appeal on Wednesday, calling for immediate assistance to protect the weakest communities already affected by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record. The agencies urged help to mitigate the impacts of this unprecedented climate event.
summary: Two UN agencies issued a powerful appeal on Wednesday. The appeal seeks immediate assistance for communities already impacted by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record.
author: UN News

title: Samarkand Summit Seeks to Improve Child Wellbeing Amid War and Climate Chaos
content:
Representatives from across the international community are meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.  
They aim to ensure children worldwide can thrive amid war, climate chaos, and other fundamental challenges.
summary: Representatives from the international community are meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to support child wellbeing. They aim to help children thrive amid war, climate chaos, and other fundamental challenges.
author: UN News

title: Migrants Pay Up to $500M in Smuggling Fees on European Sea Routes
content:
The UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the International Organization for Migration (IOM) announced on Wednesday that smuggling on European sea routes cost migrants up to half a billion dollars last year.

The agencies reported the figure as the price tag for smuggling, highlighting the significant financial burden borne by those attempting to cross European waters.
summary: The UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the UN migration office, IOM, reported that smuggling on European sea routes cost up to half a billion dollars last year. The report was released on Wednesday.
author: UN News

title: WHO scales up emergency health response in Ethiopia's Afar, Amhara and Tigray regions
content: The World Health Organization (WHO) is expanding its emergency health response in Ethiopia, focusing on the Afar, Amhara, and Tigray regions. The initiative aims to meet rising humanitarian and health needs that have grown as hostilities continue.
summary: The World Health Organization is scaling up emergency health response operations across Afar, Amhara and Tigray in Ethiopia. The effort aims to address growing humanitarian and health needs resulting from ongoing hostilities.
author: UN News

title: Live ammunition, arson mark ominous start to West Bank olive harvest
content: The opening weeks of this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank have been marked by the use of live ammunition, arson and the destruction of centuries‑old olive trees, an “ominous start” that officials say occurs amid settler attacks.
summary: The opening weeks of this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank have seen live ammunition, arson and the destruction of centuries‑old olive trees. The violence has been described as an ominous start amid settler attacks.
author: UN News

title: UN experts say fate of many DPRK nationals returned from China remains unknown
content: Three years after reports that China resumed large‑scale forcible returns of Democratic People’s Republic of Korea nationals, a panel of Human Rights Council‑appointed independent experts says serious concerns remain about the fate of many who have been sent back. The experts highlight the continued uncertainty surrounding those returnees.
summary: Three years after the reported resumption of large‑scale forcible returns of Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) nationals from China, serious concerns persist about their fate. The concerns were voiced by a group of Human Rights Council‑appointed independent experts.
author: UN News

title: Indian court orders release of Cockroach movement leaders Das and Ranka
content: An Indian court has ordered the release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, the two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement. The pair had been detained in Delhi’s Tihar jail for a week after Delhi police arrested them last week for defying restrictions on protests amid a government crackdown on youth‑led demonstrations. Their release follows the court’s decision to free the leaders who had spent the previous seven days in custody.
summary: An Indian court ordered the release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, leaders of the Cockroach Janta party movement. They had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police for defying protest restrictions.
author: Guardian World

title: Israeli military detain US and UK volunteers in West Bank including Democratic NY politician Brad Lander
content:
The Israeli military has detained roughly 80 volunteers—U.S., Israeli and British—who were assisting Palestinians with olive‑harvesting near Bethlehem. The group was taken to a police station after being held near the village of Nahalin in the West Bank.

Among those detained are New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander, several rabbis and a former Israeli deputy attorney general. Lander posted from a bus to the station, stating the volunteers were simply harvesting olives and asserting that the occupation is a crime under international law while olive‑harvesting is not a crime.
summary: Israeli military detain US and UK volunteers in West Bank including Democratic NY politician Brad Lander.
author: Guardian World

title: Taiz faces unmanageable humanitarian crisis as Houthi siege cuts water, fuel, food
content:
Oxfam aid workers in Yemen say the humanitarian situation in the besieged city of Taiz is becoming unmanageable as water, fuel and fresh food supplies run out. The city, home to more than 900,000 residents, has been largely encircled by Iran‑allied Houthi forces, which have cut off most supply routes.

This week, heavy fighting around Taiz’s old airport caused extensive damage in a densely populated residential area, further worsening conditions for the trapped population.
summary: Taiz faces unmanageable humanitarian crisis as Houthi siege cuts water, fuel, food.
author: Guardian World

title: Heidi Levine says Palestinian youths saved her after West Bank settler attack
content:
U.S. Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine said local Palestinians shielded her during a settler attack in the West Bank. While covering the olive harvest in Abu Falah, north of Ramallah, she and other journalists were knocked to the ground and repeatedly beaten by a crowd of masked settlers. Levine sustained four fractured vertebrae, two broken ribs and four puncture wounds, but Palestinian youths formed a “protective shield” that helped save her.

Levine, who criticized Prime Minister Netanyahu’s comments on the incident, vowed to return to work in the West Bank despite the injuries.
summary: US photojournalist Heidi Levine said Palestinian youths formed a protective shield that saved her after she was attacked and seriously injured by Israeli settlers in the West Bank. She suffered four fractured vertebrae, two broken ribs and four puncture wounds, but vows to return to work and criticized Netanyahu's comments on the incident.
author: Guardian World

title: Steve Witkoff flatters Putin in St Petersburg as US Trump admin spreads lies on Ukraine
content: Steve Witkoff’s flattery of the Russian leader could be just the start of a mendacious stratagem from a US president who says Moscow ‘has been fine on Ukraine’ They say the first casualty of war is truth. For the Trump administration, the road to peace with Russia now encompasses some extraordinary lies. Steve Witkoff delivered one as he sat down with Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday, aiming to close the deal on Russia’s land grab in Ukraine with the White House’s strategy of maximum pressure on Kyiv and saccharine flattery of the Kremlin.
summary: Steve Witkoff praised Vladimir Putin during a meeting in St Petersburg, which the article suggests could be the start of a US‑led misinformation campaign. The piece says the Trump administration claims Moscow has been fine on Ukraine while pursuing a strategy of maximum pressure on Kyiv.
author: Guardian World

title: Macron says Trump and other foreign leaders made 'stupid' comments on French unrest
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron said that Donald Trump and other foreign leaders have made “stupid comments” about the recent street unrest in France, describing the remarks as “unacceptable” and politically motivated. Speaking during a visit to Qatar, Macron did not name the leaders but warned that “manipulation of information” surrounding Saturday’s riots had produced such comments.

He added that the remarks were part of a broader spread of misleading information and came as France prepared for additional protests over the weekend. Macron’s criticism was directed at the perceived exploitation of the unrest by foreign officials.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron accused Donald Trump and other foreign leaders of making “stupid comments” about France’s street unrest for political gain. He said the remarks came during a visit to Qatar after Saturday’s riots and warned they were part of a manipulation of information as France prepared for further protests.
author: Guardian World

title: NSW passes human compost laws, several MPs say they will use it after death
content: Australia-first laws provide a third legal option other than burial and cremation for the treatment of bodies Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Several New South Wales MPs say they want their own bodies turned into “human compost” after Australian-first laws were passed allowing the unusual practice. The laws, passed on Wednesday, provide a third legal option other than burial and cremation for the treatment of bodies.
summary: Australian-first laws were passed on Wednesday creating a third legal option for bodies beyond burial and cremation. Several New South Wales MPs said they want their own bodies turned into “human compost” under the new legislation.
author: Guardian World

title: Sydney's south-west metro extension to open Friday 30 October
content:
The south‑west metro extension in Sydney is scheduled to open on Friday, 30 October, ending more than two years of replacement bus services for residents in that part of the city. The new line follows the closure of the former T3 heavy rail line.

New South Wales Premier Chris Minns announced the opening in a video posted to Instagram on Thursday morning. In a government statement, he said the first metro service will begin at 4:31 a.m. on the opening day.
summary: The south-west metro extension will open on Friday 30 October, ending more than two years of replacement buses after the former T3 heavy rail line closed. The first service is scheduled to start at 4.31 am, announced by NSW Premier Chris Minns.
author: Guardian World

title: NASA astronaut Luke Delaney conducts plant genetics experiments on ISS
content:
NASA astronaut Luke Delaney is conducting botany experiments aboard the International Space Station (ISS). The snapshot that appeared in the Space Photo of the Day for October 21, 2026 was captured by NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins, commander of SpaceX’s Crew‑13 mission to the ISS. In the image Delaney is seen working with petri dishes and experiment modules inside the station’s laboratory, while orbiting Earth in a vacuum of space.

Delaney’s work focuses on how plants respond to the microgravity environment. The experiments he is operating investigate the genetic responses of plants in this unique setting. By studying these genetic changes, scientists hope to better understand how plants grow when gravity is absent.

This is not the first time ISS astronauts have studied plants. Over the years, astronauts have grown peppers and other edible produce aboard the station, and have even demonstrated that moss can survive outside the ISS in the harsh environment of space. These studies form part of a broader program of biological research conducted on the station.

The ISS hosts a wide variety of life‑science experiments, from plants and animals to microscopic organisms. The data collected support human health, medical care, and Earth‑observing missions that monitor changing landforms, wildlife migration, glaciers, and natural disasters. While space remains the final frontier, the work done aboard the ISS is designed to benefit life on Earth.
summary: NASA astronaut Luke Delaney is conducting botany experiments aboard the International Space Station. The experiments, photographed by astronaut Jessica Watkins of SpaceX Crew‑13, study the genetic responses of plants in microgravity.
author: Space.com

title: Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE review: Sharp astrophotography lens costs $464
content:
The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is a full-frame prime lens designed for Sony FE and Nikon Z mounts, released in May 2023. Priced at $464 (£533), the lens is positioned as a cost-effective option for astrophotography, offering a wide-angle field of view and a fast maximum aperture. It features an all-metal body with weather-sealing, weighing 19.4 oz (550 g) and measuring 3.35 x 4.06 inches (85.2 x 103 mm). The optical construction consists of 15 elements in 12 groups, including four ED glass and three aspherical lenses, designed to deliver sharpness and high contrast with minimal distortion.

In terms of image quality, the lens performs well for night photography, with testing indicating that ISO 800 was often sufficient for correct exposure under a moonless sky. Sharpness is excellent across the frame, including the corners, even when shooting wide open at f/1.8. While vignetting is strongest at f/1.8, it reduces significantly at f/2.8 and disappears entirely by f/4. A lens profile available in Adobe Camera Raw and Lightroom completely removes this vignetting. The lens exhibits only minimal chromatic aberration and a small amount of barrel distortion. Sharpness peaks at f/8, with slight drops at f/11 and further softening due to diffraction at f/16 and f/22, though the latter apertures are noted as less relevant for astrophotography.

Functionally, the lens offers a 105.6-degree field of view on full-frame sensors, equating to a 24mm focal length on APS-C cameras. It features internal focusing, which prevents the front element from rotating or extending, making it suitable for use with filters. The lens includes a manual focusing ring wide enough for glove use, a manual aperture ring with stepped or stepless operation, two customizable Fn buttons, and an AF/MF switch. A distinctive feature is a small, illuminated color digital screen on the top of the lens that displays focus distance, aperture settings, and active Fn controls.

Additional functionality includes a USB-C port on the lens mount for power and a Bluetooth connection to the Viltrox Lens app. This app allows users to update firmware and customize the Fn buttons and the digital screen’s welcome interface. The lens has a 77 mm filter thread and a minimum focusing distance of 10.6 inches (27 cm). Autofocus is driven by an SMT stepping motor, which locks onto subjects in approximately 0.25 seconds when wide open and 0.5 seconds when stopped down.

User reviews cited in the source highlight the lens’s value, image quality, and robust build. The review concludes that the lens represents excellent value for money, balancing professional-quality build and image performance with a mid-range price. It is recommended for users seeking a wide-angle prime for astrophotography, particularly those on a budget or planning to move from APS-C to full-frame formats. The package includes the lens, a lens hood, front and rear caps, and a soft lens case.
summary: Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE review: Sharp astrophotography lens costs $464.
author: Space.com

title: Judge dismisses Morgan Carey's defamation lawsuit over Mariah Carey memoir
content: Morgan Carey sued his sister over claims in her 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey, which he said falsely portrayed him as a violent drug dealer A judge has dismissed a lawsuit from Mariah Carey’s brother, five years after he accused her of defaming him in her 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey. In the memoir, Carey described Morgan as a “sometimes drug dealing, been-in-the-system, drunk-ass brother” and called him her “ex-brother”.
summary: A judge dismissed a lawsuit filed by Morgan Carey against his sister Mariah Carey regarding claims in her 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey. Morgan Carey had alleged that the book defamed him by falsely portraying him as a violent drug dealer.
author: Guardian Culture

title: As fans reject AI-generated music, even boosters are drawing the line
content: Spotify announced the removal of approximately 50 million AI-generated songs from its user recommendations over the past year. This action reflects a broader push by streaming services, musicians, and fans to limit the presence of AI content. While artists like Grimes and A$AP Rocky embrace AI-generated material, they do not produce it themselves.
summary: As fans reject AI-generated music, even boosters are drawing the line.
author: Guardian Culture

title: ‘He had this electrical charge’: the short life and long legacy of Jason Molina, master of Americana
content: As a documentary celebrates the late US musician, friends and collaborators describe an incomparable storyteller who brought ‘myth and magic to everyday life’ Jason Molina grew up in a trailer in the working-class city of Lorain, Ohio. The city’s skyline once flickered with blue flames and a warm orange glow emanated from clattering steel mills, but by Molina’s teenage years, Lorain was in a tailspin. “Things were really on the economic decline,” says Tommy Nickoloff, Molina’s childhood friend and director of a new documentary: You Fuckers Figure It Out: A Jason Molina Story. “Nobody had any money and we were encouraged to get out. It’s a place where the American dream was born and died. And we watched it die.” Molina did indeed get out: the singer-songwriter released almost 20 studio albums and numerous EPs, primarily under the monikers Songs: Ohia and Magnolia Electric Co, spanning lo-fi to slowcore via polished Americana and alt-country. By 2009, he estimated he had written thousands of songs. But he died in 2013, aged 39, after years of alcoholism.
summary: ‘He had this electrical charge’: the short life and long legacy of Jason Molina, master of Americana.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Venter on Saracens vision as head of rugby culture and wine consultant
content:
Brendan Venter, who has transitioned from director of rugby to the role of head of rugby culture and wine consultant at Saracens, recently participated in a wine tasting session in north London. The event, which took place on a chilly Tuesday night, was framed by a reference to the Alan Partridge “smell my cheese” sketch, where wine tasting was listed as a potential activity. Venter stated that he wants people to see “the bigger picture” as he works to rebuild the club to win the Premiership.

The article notes that the shift in Venter’s job title has been a subject of discussion, with Saracens disputing that the change is a joke. Despite the rapid changes within the club, the invitation to the wine tasting was accepted, leading to an encounter that was described as either a poisoned chalice or a peace offering.
summary: Brendan Venter, now serving as head of rugby culture and wine consultant, discussed his vision for rebuilding Saracens to win the Premiership. He stated that the club wants people to see the bigger picture as it moves forward.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mark Allen reveals he made snooker return after 10-week stay in mental health clinic
content: Former world No 1 vows to show ‘fighting qualities’ ‘I see the light now that I couldn’t see before’ Mark Allen has revealed he spent 10 weeks in a mental health clinic before discharging himself to play in this week’s Northern Ireland Open. In a long statement posted on X, the 40-year-old said he was “not OK” but vowed to show his renowned “fighting qualities” as he continues his recovery. Allen’s 4-2 defeat by his friend and compatriot Jordan Brown on Tuesday was his first match since his world championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April, when he missed a black off its spot that would have given him the win.
summary: Mark Allen reveals he made snooker return after 10-week stay in mental health clinic.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Red Roses drop Kildunne to bench for Canada rematch as Mitchell seeks England reset
content:
Ellie Kildunne has been moved to the bench for England’s upcoming Test against Canada, marking one of four changes to the starting XV. The decision follows a 24-21 defeat to the Maple Leafs, which ended the Red Roses’ 41-game unbeaten streak and resulted in their first loss in four years. Emma Sing will start at full-back in Kildunne’s place for the match in Ottawa.

Head coach John Mitchell stated that Kildunne “adds huge value” and assured she “will get back” into the starting lineup. This adjustment is part of a broader effort to reset the team’s performance ahead of the third and final Test of the series.
summary: Red Roses drop Kildunne to bench for Canada rematch as Mitchell seeks England reset.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cristiano Ronaldo reduces sanction after walking out of Portugal training camp
content: He presented several arguments after Portugal walkout Inquiry chose to halve, then halve again his punishment Cristiano Ronaldo successfully fought to reduce his punishment for walking out on a Portugal training camp, after saying publicly that his sanction should be imposed “without mitigating circumstances”. After leaving the training camp in Denmark last month, Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement on social media that he should be punished as the Portuguese Football Federation saw fit and that his role as captain constituted “an aggravating factor”.
summary: Ronaldo left the Portugal training camp in Denmark last month and said on social media he should be punished without mitigating circumstances, noting his captaincy as an aggravating factor. He later presented arguments and successfully had his sanction reduced after the inquiry halved it twice.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia Collapse Leaves South Africa Near Victory
content:
Australia suffered a significant batting collapse in Gqeberha, being dismissed for 99 in their first innings and forced to follow on during the second Test against South Africa. This defeat came just one day after the home team scored over 400. The Australian team is now chasing a target while sitting at 156 for four, still trailing by 170 runs on the final day of the match.

The article describes the incident as another entry in Australia’s history of poor performances against South Africa, referencing previous low scores of 47 in Cape Town in 2011 and 85 in Hobart in 2016. The collapse was characterized by a rapid loss of wickets, with nine Australian batters falling in 38.3 overs. Notably, Nic Maddinson was dismissed in his first innings after facing only four balls on the third evening, before being out again an hour after lunch the following day.

South African bowlers Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada were highlighted for their aggressive spells, which involved high-speed deliveries that induced edges. Despite the batting failure leaving the door open for a South African victory, Australia retains a slim chance of saving the match on the final day.
summary: Australia were all out for 99 in Gqeberha after a 400+ home team score, leaving them 170 behind. The collapse, which included Nic Maddinson’s four‑ball first innings and nine wickets falling in 38.3 overs bowled by Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada, left South Africa close to victory.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Como vs Manchester United Champions League match live
content: Champions League updates for the Como v Manchester United match were posted at 5:45 pm BST, featuring a live scoreboard, the current table and commentary from Mail Simon. The report notes that the players are on the pitch and nearly ready to start. It also describes the mascot, who appears dishevelled as it comes out to pick up the match ball.
summary: Champions League updates are being provided from 5.45pm BST for the Como versus Manchester United match. The players are on the pitch and the mascot appears to be struggling with the match ball.

title: Sale player Hyron Andrews died of tear in artery around heart, autopsy finds
content: An autopsy revealed that former Sale player Hyron Andrews died of natural causes, specifically a tear in an artery around his heart. Andrews was discovered deceased at his new team’s hotel base prior to a scheduled Champions Cup match.
summary: Former Sale player Hyron Andrews was found dead at his new team's hotel base before a Champions Cup match. An autopsy determined that he died of natural causes from a tear in an artery around his heart.
author: BBC Sport

title: Amy Acton’s estranged mother used in political ad to call her a liar
content: Amy Acton’s estranged mother appeared in a political ad produced by Acton’s opponents, in which she called Acton a liar. Acton has been estranged from her mother since the age of 12. The ad has been described as disturbing for several reasons.
summary: Political opponents of Amy Acton ran an ad featuring her estranged mother, whom Acton has not spoken to since age 12. The advertisement uses the mother to accuse Acton of being a liar.

title: Trump praises Russia's release of American teacher Stephen Hubbard
content: President Trump praised Russia’s release of American teacher Stephen Hubbard following four years of wrongful imprisonment. Trump stated that Hubbard is returning home to his family and noted that the United States was not required to provide anything in return, describing it as an unprecedented situation.
summary: President Trump praised Russia's release of American teacher Stephen Hubbard after four years of wrongful imprisonment. He said Stephen is on his way home, will soon be with his family, and noted the United States was not required to give anything in return.

title: Poll: Most Americans confident in safety of routine childhood vaccines
content: A new poll from health research organization KFF indicates that most American adults remain confident in the safety of long-standing childhood vaccines. More than 80 percent of respondents expressed being “very” or “somewhat” confident in the safety of the polio vaccine and the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine. The poll also noted that public views on the COVID-19 vaccine are heavily polarized.
summary: Poll: Most Americans confident in safety of routine childhood vaccines.
author: The Hill

title: Jon Stewart Criticizes Trump's Russia Deal and Sanctions Relief
content: Jon Stewart criticized Trump’s dealings with Russia, arguing that Americans would receive little relief at the pump. He contended that Moscow would instead gain sanctions relief and another opportunity to negotiate directly with Washington on its own terms.
summary: Jon Stewart criticized Trump's dealings with Russia, stating that Americans would receive little relief at the pump. He argued that Moscow would gain sanctions relief and a direct opportunity to negotiate with Washington on its own terms.
author: The Hill

title: Cooper holds 13-point lead over Whatley in NC Senate race: Poll
content: A new Elon University poll indicates former North Carolina Governor Roy Cooper (D) maintains a 13-point lead over Republican Michael Whatley in the state’s Senate race. With less than two weeks remaining until Election Day, the survey found 52 percent of respondents favored Cooper, while 39 percent backed Whatley and 6 percent remained undecided.
summary: A new poll found former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper (D) holds a 13-point lead over his GOP opponent Michael Whatley in the state’s Senate race less than two weeks away from Election Day.
author: The Hill

title: Social Security corrects millions of SSN records for death and citizenship
content: The Social Security Administration announced on Tuesday that it has corrected millions of files in its Social Security Number database, specifically addressing death records and citizenship information. The agency stated that this update was partially achieved using the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements, or SAVE, service. Officials emphasized that maintaining the accuracy of the SSN database is essential for preserving the integrity of government services.
summary: The Social Security Administration announced it corrected millions of Social Security Number database files, including death records and citizenship information. The agency stated that it partially used the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements service to achieve these corrections.
author: The Hill

title: Supreme Court upholds gender-affirming care for federal inmates
content: The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the Trump administration must continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates in federal prisons. This decision upholds a pause on the administration's policy changes while litigation regarding the efforts to alter the policy remains ongoing.
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration must continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates in federal prisons. This decision comes as litigation over efforts to change the policy continues.
author: NPR Politics

title: Pennsylvania election official Al Schmidt prepares for midterms after 2020 threats
content: Al Schmidt is the chief election official in the state of Pennsylvania. President Trump's insults put him in danger during the 2020 ballot count. Now Schmidt talks about preparing for the midterms.
summary: Al Schmidt, the chief election official in Pennsylvania, discusses preparing for the upcoming midterm elections. He notes that President Trump's insults placed him in danger during the 2020 ballot count.

title: Trump threatens local officials with prosecution over noncitizen voter rolls, says expert
content: Election law expert Rick Hasen explains that Trump has interfered in the midterms by threatening local officials with criminal prosecution unless they remove alleged noncitizens from voter rolls.
summary: Election law expert Rick Hasen says Trump is interfering in the midterms by threatening local officials with criminal prosecution unless they remove alleged noncitizens from voter rolls. He warns that these attacks on voting system integrity could affect upcoming elections.

content: The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, thanked the prime minister for backing Jackdaw after the Tories approved it in 2022. title: Burnham approves Jackdaw gasfield, undermining Labour climate unity
content:
Zoe Williams, a columnist for The Guardian, has criticized the UK government’s approval of the Jackdaw gasfield, describing the decision as foolish and arguing it undermines the climate crisis response. Williams was attending a Guardian climate event at the Royal Geographical Society when the news broke. The event’s theme, suggested by readers, focused on public actions to address climate challenges. During the session, Shruti Suresh of the independent watchdog Global Witness urged attendees to protest against the Jackdaw and Rosebank oilfield projects.

Williams noted that the room’s mood shifted to audible dismay upon hearing the announcement, particularly after a minister for climate transition had just declared readiness for upcoming challenges. The columnist asserts that the Jackdaw approval sends a clear signal that the government does not mean what it says about ending emissions. She states that the decision will face immediate protest and legal challenge, while highlighting other hopeful initiatives such as biodiversity tracking, river protection, and rewilding.
summary: UK government minister for climate transition Steve Burnham approved the Jackdaw gasfield, a decision Zoe Williams argues undermines the government's climate commitments. The approval sparked immediate dismay and is expected to face protest and legal challenges.
author: Guardian Environment

title: EPFL Labs Explore Spinal Cord Activity via fMRI for New Therapies
content: Several EPFL laboratories are currently converging on a concept that originated as a doctoral researcher’s hunch. The team believes that functional magnetic resonance imaging of the spinal cord could potentially lead to the development of new therapies.
summary: Several EPFL labs are converging on the idea that functional magnetic resonance imaging can reveal spinal cord activity. This research, which began as a doctoral researcher's hunch, aims to unlock new therapies.
author: Medical Xpress

title: HIV remnants in BACH2 gene may promote viral persistence by altering CD4 T cells
content:
New research from the Leibniz Institute of Virology (LIV) in Hamburg indicates that HIV genetic remnants can alter immune cells, potentially promoting viral persistence. While antiretroviral therapy suppresses the virus, its genetic material remains in the body. The study suggests that when HIV integrates into specific genes, such as the BACH2 master regulator, it changes the biology of the host cell.

This integration pushes CD4 T cells toward a state characterized by long-term survival, continued division, and altered immune activity. These changes imply that viral remnants do more than simply linger, actively influencing the behavior of the cells that carry them.
summary: Research from the Leibniz Institute of Virology indicates that HIV genetic remnants integrated into specific genes like BACH2 can change the biology of the host cell. This integration pushes CD4 T cells toward a state characterized by long-term survival, continued division, and altered immune activity.

title: Brendan Nugent, charged in MP Helen Haines attack, has idiopathic transverse myelitis
content: Brendan Nugent, who is alleged to have attacked independent MP Helen Haines, appeared in court on October 21. He faces charges including dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and the federal offense of causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Nugent was also charged with cultivating and processing cannabis.
summary: Brendan Nugent, who has idiopathic transverse myelitis, appeared in court on October 21. He was charged with dangerous driving, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official.

title: Alzheimer-related brain changes may affect ALS prognosis
content: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a serious neurodegenerative disease characterized by the breakdown of nerve cells that control body muscles. The disease course varies significantly, with some patients deteriorating rapidly while others live considerably longer. This variability makes it difficult to assess early on how the disease will progress.
summary: Alzheimer-related changes in the brain may affect the prognosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The disease course varies greatly, making it difficult to assess early how the condition will progress.

title: Parents share how to handle complicated feelings of not enjoying parenting
content: While parenting is frequently described as one of life’s most rewarding experiences, many parents acknowledge that it involves difficult moments. For some, these challenging periods can feel almost constant.
summary: Many parents report that parenting is full of difficult moments that can seem almost constant. This contradicts the common belief that it is one of life's most rewarding experiences.

title: Menopause and Exercise: Experts Explain What Works
content: While hot flashes and night sweats often dominate menopause discussions, experts highlight less visible physiological changes. Muscle mass gradually decreases and is replaced by fat, while bone density declines. Additionally, the body requires fewer calories to function daily during this period.
summary: Hot flashes and night sweats dominate conversations about menopause. Other important changes include muscle loss to fat, bone density loss, and reduced caloric needs.

content: A new study published in Science Immunology suggests that a prominent protein on most human cells may be key to understanding human susceptibility to pathogenic bacteria and viruses, including HIV. The research was led by scientists from Purdue University and the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.
summary: A new study led by researchers at Purdue University and the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute was published in Science Immunology. title: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley earn $52B, hold 80% of equity trading market
content: Wall Street’s Big Three, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley, have generated $52 billion in equity trading revenue this year. The firms have captured approximately 80% of the market, a position attributed to rising margin lending to hedge funds.

title: France 10‑year bond yield tops 5% as unrest and budget deadlock spook markets
content:
French borrowing costs have surged past 5% for the first time in 24 years, driven by political instability and the government’s inability to agree on a delayed budget. This spike in yields reflects growing anxiety in financial markets, which were further unsettled by recent violent street protests that left some civic buildings smouldering.

As the second largest economy in the eurozone, France faces significant pressure from these economic headwinds. The combination of civil unrest and fiscal uncertainty has triggered a fresh wave of selling, pushing the interest rate on ten-year government bonds to historic levels.
summary: The yield on France's 10‑year government bonds rose above 5%, the highest level in 24 years, amid the failure to pass a budget and fallout from violent street protests. Continued unrest, with some civic buildings still smouldering, prompted fresh selling that pushed the yield higher on bonds issued by the eurozone's second‑largest economy.
author: Guardian Business

title: Africa's bats face climate change and land‑use threats
content: Climate change and land-use changes pose the two greatest threats to wildlife by altering the environments necessary for animal survival. Understanding how species respond to these pressures is essential for developing effective conservation strategies.
summary: Climate change and changes in land use are the two biggest threats to wildlife, including Africa's bats. Understanding how species respond to these pressures is essential for conservation planning.

title: New tool tracks viral RNA in live infected cells in real time
content:
Joyce Jose, an associate professor of biochemistry and molecular biology at Penn State, notes that viruses hijack host cell machinery to replicate out of sight. She explains that understanding these dynamics is the first step toward developing effective antiviral strategies to stop infections. However, scientists have largely been left in the dark because limited tools exist to study how viruses move in space and time inside live infected cells.

To address this gap, a new two-in-one tool has been developed to track viral RNA inside live infected cells in real time. This innovation provides the necessary capability to observe viral movement within living systems, offering a critical resource for advancing antiviral research.
summary: A new two-in-one tool allows scientists to track viral RNA inside live infected cells in real time. This development addresses the lack of tools available to study how viruses move in space and time within host cells.
author: Phys.org

title: War trauma shapes CEOs' business decisions decades later
content: Eun Hye Jo and Jenny Jung-Wha Lee, accounting professors at the Costello College of Business at George Mason University Korea, argue that childhood war trauma continues to influence business decisions decades later. They contend that these early experiences have long-lasting reverberations that significantly shape the decision-making processes of CEOs.
summary: Accounting professors Eun Hye Jo and Jenny Jung-Wha Lee argue that childhood experiences of war have long-lasting effects on business decisions. This trauma continues to influence the decision-making processes of CEOs decades after the events.

title: Poor ocean conditions leave murrelet chicks exposed to nest predators for longer
content: A new study by Oregon State University scientists indicates that unfavorable ocean conditions cause marbled murrelet chicks to remain in the nest longer. This extended nesting period leaves the Pacific Northwest seabirds more vulnerable to predation.
summary: Less favorable ocean conditions cause marbled murrelet chicks to take longer to leave the nest. This extended time makes the chicks more vulnerable to predation, according to a study by Oregon State University scientists.

content: A new survey by the University of Michigan’s Detroit Metro Area Communities Study, conducted with Outlier Media, indicates that more than one in four Detroit adults cannot easily produce up-to-date proof of U.S. citizenship matching their current name. The findings suggest that proposed additional identification requirements for voting could disenfranchise a significant portion of the city’s adult population.

content: An international research team, which includes members from the University of Michigan, has reported observations from the Hubble Space Telescope. These findings suggest that supernova winds may not have played the significant role previously thought in the cosmic reionization process, potentially altering the scientific understanding of this early universe transition.
summary: An international team of researchers, including members from the University of Michigan, has revealed surprising results from Hubble observations. These findings could rewrite our understanding of a key transition in the early universe.

content: Researchers from the Penn State College of Earth and Mineral Sciences report that natural gas leaks are a significant source of methane emissions in cities, though pinpointing their specific locations and causes remains difficult. The team notes that methane, the main chemical component of natural gas and a potent greenhouse gas, has historically been undercounted or omitted in emissions estimates.

content: The concept that a single individual’s poor conduct can negatively impact an entire group, often described as one bad apple spoiling the barrel, has received new scientific support. title: Some climate damage is now unavoidable even if we clean up our act
content:
The United Nations has acknowledged that limiting global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels will likely require an "overshoot, peak, decline" strategy, where temperatures exceed the threshold before cooling back down by 2100. This development highlights the critical question of whether climate damage is reversible. While scientists are racing to determine the extent of lasting harm, the situation presents a mix of potential recovery and irreversible loss.

Some positive indicators exist regarding the resilience of certain systems. Important land carbon sinks, such as the Amazon rainforest, appear capable of recovering from short-term climate shocks. Additionally, there is a possibility of resuscitating the AMOC, a vital ocean current, following a climate-induced collapse, although the process is described as difficult.

However, significant portions of climate impact are now locked in, regardless of immediate emission reductions. The Thwaites glacier in Antarctica is considered beyond saving even if ocean-driven melting were to stop immediately. Consequently, substantial future sea-level rise is inevitable. While this outcome is not a reason for despair, it underscores that passing the 1.5°C mark will leave lasting scars. The text emphasizes that while global cooling may eventually be achieved, the overshoot years will not be unscathed, making current emission cuts essential for the future.
summary: Uros Arsic/AFP via Getty Images Thermometers, at least traditionally, don’t remember. Mercury expands in response to heat energy, and the red line rises.

title: El Niño causes falling sea levels that threaten mangroves and corals
content: Sea levels in the eastern Pacific are rising, while they are falling around Australia and the Coral Triangle. This shift, attributed to El Niño, is leaving some mangroves and corals high and dry.
summary: Sea levels are falling around Australia and the Coral Triangle because of El Niño. This leaves some mangroves and corals high and dry.

title: NASA Perseverance rover breaks off‑world driving record, surpassing Opportunity
content:
NASA’s Perseverance rover has broken the off‑world driving record, becoming the vehicle that has traveled the greatest distance on another planet. Using its advanced self‑driving system, Perseverance surpassed Opportunity’s 28.06‑mile record in just five and a half years, a milestone that previously required nearly 15 years.

The rover is now examining some of the solar system’s oldest rocks and looking for evidence of ancient Martian environments that may once have supported life.
summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has traveled farther on another world than any vehicle before, breaking the off‑world driving record. Its advanced self‑driving system let it exceed Opportunity’s 28.06‑mile record in five and a half years while it studies ancient Martian rocks for clues about past habitability.

title: Scientists reverse 60 years of aging in human cells
content: Scientists have successfully reversed over 60 years of cellular aging in a laboratory setting by converting blood cells from an 80-year-old into neural stem cells with a molecular age under 20. This breakthrough provides a novel method for studying the mechanisms of cellular rejuvenation and may aid researchers in understanding age-related conditions like Alzheimer's disease.
summary: Scientists converted blood cells from an 80-year-old into neural stem cells with a molecular age of less than 20. This discovery provides a new method for investigating cellular rejuvenation and understanding age-related diseases like Alzheimer's.

content: A study of over 460,000 Americans found no overall association between ultra-processed foods and increased colorectal cancer risk, challenging common assumptions. The research indicated that while processed meat was linked to higher cancer incidence, ultra-processed whole grains and dairy products were associated with lower incidence rates.
summary: A massive study of more than 460,000 Americans found that ultra-processed foods were not associated with increased colorectal cancer risk overall. The study noted that processed meat was linked to higher cancer incidence, while ultra-processed whole grains and dairy products were associated with lower incidence.

content: A new study tracking 13 astronauts indicates that the human heart may be well-equipped for a Mars journey, particularly with regular exercise during spaceflight. Researchers observed that astronauts’ hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and managed simulated Martian gravity without major issues, providing new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.
summary: Researchers tracked 13 astronauts and found that their hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and could handle simulated Martian gravity without major problems, especially with regular exercise. The study suggests the human heart may be well equipped for a journey to Mars, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.

title: Too Much RNA Damages Mitochondria, Starving Cells of Energy
content: Scientists have found that an excess of RNA, including messenger RNA (mRNA), can directly damage mitochondria—the cell’s energy‑producing structures—without involving the immune system. This new study suggests that such RNA‑induced mitochondrial disruption may help explain cellular damage seen in viral infections and certain aging‑related diseases.
summary: Scientists discovered that excess RNA, including messenger RNA, can directly damage mitochondria, the cell's energy-producing structures. This finding may explain how viral infections and aging-related diseases harm cells.

title: Penn State Study Finds 4-Minute Daily Strength Training Boosts Mobility in Seniors
content: A new Penn State study found that just four minutes of daily strength training can significantly improve mobility and physical function in older adults. After 12 weeks, participants showed meaningful gains in balance, leg strength, and the ability to stand up from a chair—key factors for maintaining independence and reducing fall risk.
summary: The study, conducted at Penn State, tested a four‑minute daily strength training program over 12 weeks with older adults. Participants showed significant improvements in balance, leg strength, and the ability to stand up from a chair.

title: 160‑meter asteroid creates Silverpit Crater, triggers 100‑meter tsunami in North Sea
content:
Scientists have finally solved a decades‑long mystery beneath the North Sea.  They confirmed that the Silverpit Crater, buried 700 meters below the seabed, was formed when a 160‑meter‑wide asteroid struck the Earth about 43 to 46 million years ago.

The impact blasted a curtain of rock and water 1.5 kilometers into the air and triggered a tsunami more than 100 meters high—roughly 330 feet—making the event one of the most powerful in the region’s geological history.
summary: Scientists confirmed the Silverpit Crater, buried 700 meters below the seabed, was formed by a 160‑meter‑wide asteroid that struck Earth about 43 to 46 million years ago. The impact lifted a curtain of rock and water 1.5 kilometers high and generated a tsunami exceeding 100 meters.

title: More than a million mice used in Australian research annually, ‘overdue’ study finds
content:
A nationwide survey released today shows that more than one million mice and nearly 47,000 rats are used each year in Australian scientific research. The data, compiled by veterinarian Dr Malcolm France, represents the first comprehensive count of rodents employed in the country’s research facilities.

France described the count as “an overdue first step” toward publishing national statistics for all animals used in research, including fish, rabbits, birds and monkeys. Advocates say that having such national data can help boost public trust in science.
summary: More than a million mice and nearly 47,000 rats are used in Australian scientific research each year, according to the first nationwide count. Dr Malcolm France, a veterinarian who compiled the data, called the release an overdue first step toward publishing national statistics for all animals used in research, including fish, rabbits, birds and monkeys.

title: Expert Identifies Skeleton in Westminster Abbey Sarcophagus as 11th‑Century Abbot
content:
An archaeologist has announced that the skeleton found inside a Roman sarcophagus unearthed on the grounds of Westminster Abbey is likely the remains of an 11th‑century abbot. The coffin, inscribed to Valerius Amandinus, had long been the subject of speculation about its occupant.

The expert’s identification resolves the long‑standing “who‑is‑it” question, concluding that the unknown man was a medieval abbot rather than a Roman figure. This finding clarifies the identity of the remains and ends the mystery surrounding the sarcophagus.
summary: An archaeologist says the skeleton inside a Roman sarcophagus at Westminster Abbey, inscribed to Valerius Amandinus, is likely the remains of an 11th‑century abbot. The skeleton of an unknown man was discovered within the sarcophagus unearthed in the Abbey grounds.

title: NASA’s CASALS Lidar Fills Gaps in Earth’s 3D Surface Mapping
content:
NASA researchers at the Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) have developed the Concurrent Artificially-intelligent Spectrometry Lidar System (CASALS) to address significant gaps in current space-based laser measurements of Earth’s surface. Existing orbital instruments measure forests and terrain in narrow lines, leaving millions of acres unmapped between these tracks. Built with support from NASA’s Earth Science Technology Office (ESTO), CASALS blends machine learning with an ultra-compact lidar to create continuous, three-dimensional topographical renderings. The instrument’s primary innovation is its non-mechanical steering method, which uses light wavelength rather than moving mirrors to generate a continuous swath of data.

John Yorks, a physical research scientist at GSFC and Principal Investigator for CASALS, explained that the system utilizes a fast-pulsing, tunable “seed” laser centered at 1040 nanometers. This laser rapidly cycles through 256 unique wavelengths as it passes through a transmission grating, an optical component featuring a microscopic pattern of ridges. Due to the physics of diffraction, the grating bends light at slightly different angles based on its exact wavelength, naturally steering each of the 256 pulses into distinct positions across the flight path. This approach eliminates the need for heavy, failure-prone motorized mirrors, drastically reducing the instrument’s size, weight, and power requirements while enhancing reliability for the space environment.

A second key innovation is the detector array, which operates at an 80% Quantum Efficiency (QE). This high efficiency allows the instrument to convert incoming photons into electrical signals with minimal loss, enabling CASALS to detect weaker return signals from darker surfaces or through dense vegetation. In November 2024, an airborne prototype of CASALS flew aboard NASA’s B200 King Air aircraft, producing science-quality datasets on its first campaign. During a flight over the Great Cypress Swamp in Delaware, the instrument captured detailed imagery showing tree canopy tops in green, the ground in purple, and near-ground vegetation in blue.

Yorks noted that the instrument performed well from its first flight, exceeding team expectations. Flying at an altitude of roughly five kilometers, CASALS achieved a 22-centimeter horizontal resolution, allowing it to distinguish individual tree branches and subtle changes in ground elevation. Yorks stated that the system provides fine details of vegetation structure and surface topography. The team is currently preparing for further development, with plans to widen the instrument’s swath and add onboard data processing software before creating a space-ready prototype.

The next scheduled flight for the airborne prototype is planned for summer 2027 as part of the Airborne Surface, Cryosphere, Ecosystem, and Nearshore Topography (ASCENT) campaign. The project is supported by NASA’s Decadal Survey Incubation (DSI) program, NASA’s Instrument Incubation Program (IIP), NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University. If successful, CASALS could become the first spaceborne lidar capable of mapping Earth’s forests and terrain as continuous three-dimensional swaths rather than isolated profiles.
summary: NASA’s CASALS instrument uses wavelength steering to create continuous 3D swaths, filling the gaps left by traditional line‑by‑line lidar. An airborne prototype flew aboard a B200 King Air in November 2024, producing science‑quality data and demonstrating the system’s performance at 22‑centimeter resolution.

title: Jessica Watkins Conducts 3D Bioprinting Cartilage Research on ISS
content:
On Oct. 9, 2026, NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins worked inside the Kibo laboratory module’s Life Science Glovebox on the International Space Station. She was part of the InSPA‑Auxilium Bioprinter‑Cell Printing investigation.

Watkins safely mixed living cell samples with a bioink and filled a special cartridge with the resulting cell‑ink mixture. The experiment aimed to 3D‑bioprint cartilage tissue in microgravity.

The research seeks to produce cartilage of higher quality than that made on Earth. Successful results could advance biomanufacturing of cartilage for patients on Earth and for crew members on long‑duration space missions.
summary: NASA astronaut and Expedition 75 flight engineer Jessica Watkins mixed living cell samples with bioink in the Kibo Life Science Glovebox on Oct. 9, 2026. The experiment, part of the InSPA‑Auxilium Bioprinter‑Cell Printing investigation, seeks to produce higher‑quality 3D‑printed cartilage in microgravity to benefit Earth patients and long‑duration space crews.
