title: Perseverance rover drives 45.22 km, longest distance on another celestial body
content:
NASA’s Perseverance rover has established a new record for the farthest distance driven on another celestial body. On Sol 2006, which corresponds to October 11, 2026, the rover’s odometer reached 45.22 kilometers (28.10 miles). To celebrate this achievement, the rover’s engineering twin on Earth received a plaque from Guinness World Records. The milestone was documented by an image taken with the rover’s Left Navigation Camera at a local mean solar time of 14:40:39, showing the wheel tracks from the record-breaking drive.

The path to this record involved a period of intensive scientific activity. Approximately two months prior, on Sol 1947, the odometer was only about 200 meters from the milestone, a distance that could have been covered in a single drive using Autonomous Navigation (AutoNav). However, the rover remained in a scientifically significant area, utilizing short drives to perform rock abrasions and proximity science on ancient rock outcrops. When the rover eventually departed for a new site, it surpassed the distance record.

Achieving this distance required the engineering team to adapt to challenging Martian terrain, including dense boulder fields and steep slopes. Following thousands of simulations, the team adjusted the rover’s operational parameters to better handle tough conditions. These changes included raising the tilt limit to 24 degrees and reducing the required clearance under the rover’s belly pan to 20 centimeters (about 7.9 inches). Additionally, the team updated the braking software to avoid rock hazards, nearly doubled the steer motor current limits, and implemented “dynamic slip tables” in the flight software to model expected slip. The team also utilized cross-slope driving techniques to better anchor the wheels on exposed bedrock.

A significant technological advancement supporting these longer drives is the autonomous capability known as onboard Global Localization (GBLC). This system repurposes the high-speed commercial processor from the Ingenuity Helicopter Base Station to compare ground and orbital imagery, allowing the rover to autonomously determine its location in global coordinates at the end of a drive. This capability functions similarly to GPS, enabling Perseverance to travel longer distances without human intervention.

Because this commercial processor is not hardened against the radiation environment on Mars, the team developed a software-based approach to mitigate the effects of “transient bit flips” in memory. The lack of a global magnetosphere and a thin atmosphere on Mars provides little shielding from radiation. Looking ahead, the team is exploring the use of generative AI to help propose solutions for steering AutoNav along strategic paths, aiming to plan more activities with fewer resources as the rover continues to climb higher along the crater rim.
summary: Perseverance rover drives 45.22 km, longest distance on another celestial body.
author: NASA News

title: NASA to Flyover University of Alabama Game, Invite Fans to Experience Zone
content:
NASA’s Freedom 250 F‑5 team, led by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, will perform a flyover during the national anthem at an NFL game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers at Huntington Bank Field on September 27, 2026. The same team will also participate in the agency’s Inspiration Tour, conducting a flyover at the University of Alabama vs. Texas A&M football game in Tuscaloosa on Saturday, October 24. Isaacman will pilot one of three F‑5 fighter jets during the Tuscaloosa flyover, underscoring NASA’s contributions to aeronautics and its commitment to advancing aviation technologies.

Ahead of the October 24 game, members of the news media are invited to the NASA Experience Zone on Champions Lane. Isaacman will hold a media opportunity at 11 a.m. CDT, and media interested in attending must confirm their attendance by 12 p.m. Friday, October 23 with Lance D. Davis at lance.Davis@nasa.gov. The Experience Zone, supported by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, will be open to the public from 10:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. CDT, and no game ticket is required.

Visitors to the Experience Zone can meet NASA team members and explore exhibits highlighting the agency’s Artemis campaign and efforts to return astronauts to the Moon. Displays include an inflatable Space Launch System (SLS) rocket, Starship and Blue Moon human landing systems, information about NASA internship opportunities, and photo opportunities featuring NASA exhibits.

The Inspiration Tour will conclude with MAX POWER, a public exposition of American air and space innovation, on Saturday, November 7, and Sunday, November 8, near the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The multi‑day, family‑friendly event celebrates America’s 250th anniversary and showcases next‑generation aircraft, spacecraft, autonomous vehicles, and technologies that will shape the future of transportation in air and space. For more information about MAX POWER and NASA’s missions, visit https://www.nasa.gov/maxpower.
summary: NASA’s Freedom 250 F-5 team, including NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, performs a flyover during the national anthem at an NFL game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers at Huntington Bank Field, Sept. 27, 2026, in Cleveland.
author: NASA News

title: The Download Launches Impossible Issue Spotlighting Lunar AI and Synthetic Blood
content:
MIT Technology Review has announced the release of its “Impossible” print issue, described as the final edition of 2026. The publication focuses on ambitious technological endeavors, including attempts to create synthetic blood, build lunar cities, and achieve cognitive immortality. The issue also investigates artificial intelligence’s capacity to refuse requests, bionic eyes that restore sight, and the development of blended meat. Additionally, it reviews six technologies that have long been anticipated but not yet realized. The editors state that the issue honors scientists and engineers who pursue daring projects to make life better, safer, and healthier.

A key story in the newsletter highlights Astrolab’s FLIP lunar rover, which is scheduled to launch to the moon as early as next month. The rover carries a computer capable of running large language models (LLMs), marking the first time such AI software will operate in a lunar environment. The mission aims to test whether LLMs can facilitate greater autonomy and real-time decision-making despite extreme temperatures and cosmic radiation.

Another featured article discusses research conducted in Alaska’s Denali National Park, where a 2013 lightning fire burned nearly 35,000 acres and removed the insulating layer that preserves permafrost. Scientists are using this event to study how fires impact permafrost and carbon storage. Their findings indicate that warming temperatures fuel fires, which cause permafrost to thaw and release greenhouse gases, creating a cascading feedback loop that accelerates further warming.

In the AI sector, the newsletter reports on a 26,000-word blog post by Nick Cammarata, a researcher at AI startup Goodfire. Cammarata claims that LLMs may be easier to understand, monitor, and control than previously thought. While the post has generated significant industry attention, the article notes that not everyone is convinced of these findings. MIT Technology Review interviewed Cammarata the day after the post was published to discuss his research and the skepticism surrounding it.

The newsletter also summarizes several other recent developments. Elon Musk reportedly ordered a recent Starlink slowdown in Ukraine, which hampered drone strikes and air defenses. Additionally, SpaceX and Tesla have begun merger discussions, with special committees formed to evaluate a potential deal that could combine their AI and manufacturing plans. Other reported news includes Ukraine carrying out the world’s first drone evacuation of a soldier, Meta pausing Muse sharing after private chats were exposed online, and more than 1,000 mathematicians pledging to avoid AI companies and tools.

The edition concludes with a segment on defense technology, specifically a high-powered microwave weapon developed by startup Epirus. The US armed forces are interested in this technology as a method to disable drones in large numbers. The device pushes out kilowatts of power to disrupt drone circuits, offering a cost-efficient alternative to traditional counter-drone measures.
summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Introducing: the Impossible issue We wanted our last print edition of 2026 to include a slate of stories that check in on impossible ideas.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Hackers Use Anthropic’s Claude AI to Facilitate Cyber Attacks
content: Hackers worldwide are increasingly employing agentic AI to conduct attacks, according to recent reports. They are also manipulating tools such as Anthropic’s Claude, using them to facilitate the execution of their criminal activities.
summary: Hackers around the world are employing agentic AI to conduct cyber attacks. They are manipulating tools such as Anthropic’s Claude to assist in their crimes.
author: Wired

title: PHP Foundation Reveals Two Serious Vulnerabilities Threatening Millions of Websites
content:
The PHP Foundation has announced the discovery of two serious vulnerabilities that could affect millions of websites.  

Security experts caution that if these flaws are not patched promptly, the consequences could be severe.
summary: The PHP Foundation has identified two serious vulnerabilities that could impact millions of websites. Security experts warn that failure to quickly patch the flaws could have dire consequences.
author: Wired

title: Nvidia’s Huang Unveils DSX Pod Plug‑In Data Center at Berlin GTC
content: At Nvidia’s GTC in Berlin, Jensen Huang introduced the company’s new plug‑in data center, the DSX Pod. Huang said the DSX Pod would be the key to addressing Europe’s lag in AI infrastructure. He also mentioned the company’s work on autonomous humanoid robotics.
summary: At Nvidia’s GTC in Berlin, Jensen Huang unveiled the DSX Pod plug‑in data center, which he said would help address Europe’s AI infrastructure lag. He also mentioned autonomous humanoid robotics.
author: Wired

title: Blink Launches 4K, Pan-Tilt Security Cameras and Battery-Powered Spotlight Models
content:
Amazon has announced a new lineup of Blink security cameras that expands the company’s offerings with its first 4 K, pan‑tilt models and battery‑powered spotlight models. The update promises higher resolution and an extended monitoring range compared to Blink’s existing Mini 2 K, Mini 2 K Plus and Outdoor 2 K Plus cameras.

The new lineup includes the Outdoor 2 K XR Plus and Mini Pant‑Tilt 2 K Plus, as well as the Spotlight Cam 2 K Plus, Mini 4 K Plus and the Frontier XR Plus. These devices are designed to meet a variety of security needs, offering improved image quality and broader coverage for property protection.

A key highlight is the $199.99 Frontier XR Plus trail camera. Built for expansive properties that would normally require multiple cameras, it can cover up to 7,000 feet with a clear line of sight.
summary: Blink is launching a new lineup of security cameras, including its first 4K pan‑tilt models and battery‑powered spotlight models. The new lineup offers higher resolution and extended range, with the $199.99 Blink Frontier XR Plus trail camera covering up to 7,000 feet.
author: The Verge

title: Apple says only limited iPhone Duo units will be available in stores
content: Apple says it will have "limited" iPhone Duo models for sale in stores, according to a report from Reuters. The iPhone Duo launches on Friday, October 23rd, but online preorders quickly sold out, with some delivery estimates extending into next year. "On Friday morning, our teams look forward ​to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo ​and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," Apple said in a statement to Reuters. "Apple Stores will ‌have ⁠limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we're working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible." The iPhon …
summary: Apple announced that only a limited number of iPhone Duo models will be available for walk‑in customers at its retail stores. The iPhone Duo launched on Friday, October 23, and online pre‑orders sold out quickly, with some deliveries extending into next year.
author: The Verge

title: Samsung Odyssey G80HF 27‑inch 5K monitor sells for $599 with 180Hz gaming
content:
Samsung’s 27‑inch Odyssey G80HF 5K monitor is positioned as a budget‑friendly option for gamers who want a high‑resolution screen without breaking the bank. The model is available for $599.99 at Amazon and B&H Photo, a price that is $100 lower than its best listed price. The monitor’s Fast IPS panel can run in two modes: a 5K resolution at up to 180 Hz or a 1440p resolution at up to 360 Hz. Samsung advertises Nvidia G‑Sync compatibility and AMD FreeSync Premium support to keep the refresh rate synchronized with the graphics card’s output.

Connectivity on the G80HF includes a single DisplayPort 2.1 (bandwidth not specified), two HDMI 2.1 ports, and a USB hub that offers two USB‑A 3.2 Gen 1 ports for charging or connecting accessories. One of the monitor’s highlighted features is its one‑millisecond response time, a specification that is common on lower‑priced gaming displays but less frequent on 5K monitors at this price point.

For comparison, LG’s 27‑inch UltraGear evo 5K Mini LED monitor sells for $799.99. It offers more dimming zones for a more accurate picture, a higher maximum brightness, and a USB‑C video input that can deliver 90 W of power to charge a device while it is in use. The UltraGear’s dual‑mode refresh rates are 165 Hz and 330 Hz, which are lower than the Samsung’s 180 Hz and 360 Hz options, but the article notes that this difference is not considered a major drawback.

Other promotions highlighted in the article include a Grand Theft Auto VI preorder bundle that gives a $10 discount on a gaming gift card when the game is added to a Best Buy bundle. The bundle also contains other titles such as Gears of War: E‑Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. The remake of Demon’s Souls is available on the PlayStation Store for $13.49 as a digital deluxe edition, with the sale ending on November 4th on the West Coast or 2:59 AM ET on November 5th on the East Coast. Additionally, Ugreen’s Nexode Pro multi‑port wall charger is listed at $59.99 on Amazon and Ugreen, offering up to 160 W of total power with four USB‑C ports (each up to 140 W when a single device is plugged in) and one USB‑A port. The charger features folding prongs and a rotating display.
summary: There are quite a few 5K monitors out there. Many of them are designed to appeal to Mac users who are looking for cheaper Studio Display alternatives without giving up the pixel-dense 218ppi screen.
author: The Verge

title: Google launches Conversational Gemini navigation on Apple CarPlay
content:
Google has expanded its Gemini AI assistant, first launched on Android Auto last year, to Apple CarPlay. The conversational Gemini navigation feature is live today for drivers in the United States, and Google says a global rollout is also under way, though regional details have not been provided.

The update lets CarPlay users speak to the voice assistant within Google Maps for hands‑free assistance while driving. Users can ask multi‑step questions, such as for place recommendations and then request directions that avoid toll roads. Google noted the addition comes roughly 12 months after the Android Auto launch.
summary: Google launches Conversational Gemini navigation on Apple CarPlay.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Music launches new logo, updated wordmark and sound in rebrand
content:
Apple announced a rebrand of Apple Music, unveiling a new logo, an updated wordmark and a fresh sound track. The redesign follows a redesigned wordmark shown in a video and an updated app icon that appeared in the iOS 27.2 beta. The new sound was created by British producer Fred Again in collaboration with Nest Acoustics.

In a promotional video, Apple explains that the rebrand “wanted sound to create the visuals,” featuring the music‑note logo and wordmark submerged in water that reacts to the audio. The video demonstrates the water‑based animation of the new visual identity.
summary: Apple officially introduced a rebrand of Apple Music with a new logo, updated wordmark and a new sound. The new sound was composed by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics and was shown in a video and an iOS 27.2 beta app icon.
author: The Verge

title: Supernatural VR fitness game relaunches with Early Access on Meta Horizon Store
content:
Supernatural, the fitness VR game previously supported by Meta, has relaunched as an independent app with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store. The new version launches today with thousands of “remastered” workouts and a selection of new routines, and additional content is slated for release.

The app’s subscription price has risen from $9.99 per month to $20 per month or $200 per year. Starting next week, Supernatural will add new workouts each week, and the developers say more back‑catalog favorites will return in the coming weeks and months.
summary: Supernatural, a fitness VR game, has relaunched with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store, offering thousands of remastered workouts and some new ones starting today. The independent app’s subscription price has risen to $20 per month or $200 per year, and new workouts will be added weekly beginning next week.
author: The Verge

title: Optimizer newsletter author Victoria Song records 24 blood draws this year
content: Your blood, for “immortality.” | Image: Cath Virgina / The Verge, Getty Images This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they're going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here. It's an overcast Saturday morning when I give my 12th vial of blood for testing in six weeks. It's my 24th this year. At this point, I feel like a pro. I schedule these blood draws first thing in the morning so I don't get hangry, download the requisition papers ahead of time, avoid strenuous exercise for the 24 hours prior, and make sure to drink a glass of water beforehand so my teeny veins are easier for the phlebotomist to f …
summary: Optimizer is a weekly newsletter from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that examines new health gadgets and potions. In a recent issue, Song notes she gave her 12th vial of blood in six weeks, bringing her total to 24 draws this year as part of testing for “immortality.”
author: The Verge

title: EA shuts down BioWare studio and cancels upcoming Mass Effect game
content:
Electronic Arts confirmed that BioWare, the studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, is shutting down. In an internal announcement, EA also said it will not continue development of the next Mass Effect game that was in progress. The company is laying off roughly 400 staff members, Bloomberg reports.

The shutdown comes after EA completed a $55 billion privatization deal in August. “BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role‑playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” said Cam Weber, EA president.
summary: BioWare is shutting down and EA announced it will not continue development on the next Mass Effect game that was in the works. The closure includes laying off around 400 staffers and comes after EA went private in a $55 billion deal that closed in August.
author: The Verge

title: Blacksmith reaches $1 billion valuation in $66 million Series C led by Sequoia
content: Blacksmith, a platform that enables companies to build and test AI code more effectively, announced a $66 million Series C financing round led by Sequoia. The investment values Blacksmith at $1 billion, giving the company unicorn status.
summary: Blacksmith, a platform that lets companies build and test AI code, announced a $66 million Series C funding round. The round was led by Sequoia and values the company at $1 billion.
author: TechCrunch

title: Modern Warfare 4 praised for narrative-driven campaign set in South Korea invasion
content:
Modern Warfare 4’s campaign has been highlighted for its narrative focus, positioning character and consequence at the core of its large‑scale battles. The game’s story unfolds during an invasion of South Korea by its northern neighbour, featuring a fictional authoritarian regime led by a new ruler who deploys a powerful experimental weapon as the opening move of the attack.

Players assume the role of Park Hyun Jun, a conscripted South Korean soldier. Alongside a small unit of similarly inexperienced grunts, Jun is thrust into a firestorm of burning cities and enemy paratroopers. The setting and storytelling have drawn praise, with some writers suggesting the campaign may rank among the best Call of Duty single‑player experiences in at least six years.
summary: The upcoming Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign is being hailed as the series' strongest in at least six years. It places players in the role of Park Hyun Jun, a conscripted South Korean soldier caught in a fictional invasion of South Korea by its northern neighbor.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Best Amazon Kindle models in the UK for all budgets and needs
content:
A new guide to Amazon’s Kindle range in the United Kingdom recommends specific models for a variety of reading needs and price points. The article notes that the lineup now includes options with colour screens, devices designed for note‑taking, and child‑friendly versions, alongside models aimed at tighter budgets.

The guide highlights that Kindles can hold thousands of titles while weighing as little as 158 g, and it points out that the e‑readers avoid many of the “time‑wasting” features common on phones and tablets. Amazon has sold Kindles in the UK for more than 15 years, and the 2024 update introduced colour displays as the most significant addition to the existing range.
summary: Amazon offers several Kindle e‑readers in the UK, including colour‑screen, note‑taking, child‑friendly and budget options. The lineup, available for more than 15 years, received its biggest update in 2024 with the addition of colour screens.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Prix Pascal de Littérature IA prize launched for AI‑co‑written fiction
content: A new literary award, the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA, has been launched to recognize fiction co‑written with large‑language‑model AI tools. Following months of controversy about AI use by winners of other prestigious awards, the prize invites manuscript submissions that involve AI assistance and promises publication for the winning entry.
summary: The Prix Pascal de Littérature IA prize was launched this week to reward fiction written with the help of large language models. The award invites submissions of manuscripts co‑written with AI tools and promises publication for the winner.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Macron urges caution in Gulf, clinches key gas deal with Qatar on state visit
content: French president concludes his state visit by reinforcing the strategic partnership with Qatar. He declares his Gulf tour objectives achieved after securing a crucial gas deal with Qatar as he seeks to lower tensions over living costs in France.
summary: French President Macron concluded his state visit by reinforcing the strategic partnership with Qatar. He said the tour’s objectives were met after securing a crucial gas deal with Qatar, while urging extreme caution in the Gulf and seeking to ease living‑cost tensions in France.
author: Euronews

title: Devotees walk on fire for luck at Malaysia's Nine Emperor Gods Festival in Kuala Pilah
content: At Malaysia’s Nine Emperor Gods Festival in Kuala Pilah, devotees walked across burning embers seeking good luck. The ceremony was accompanied by fireworks, a lion dance and blessings offered at a local temple.
summary: Devotees walked on fire for good luck at Malaysia’s Nine Emperor Gods Festival. The celebration included fireworks, a lion dance and blessings at a temple in Kuala Pilah.
author: Euronews

title: Zelenskyy backs freezing front line as first step toward Ukraine ceasefire
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says the first step toward a ceasefire should be a freeze of the front line. He adds that Kyiv must be included in any talks and is seeking security guarantees from Washington and European allies. The statement comes while a dispute over slowed SpaceX satellite services continues.
summary: Zelenskyy backs freezing front line as first step toward Ukraine ceasefire.
author: Euronews

title: Russian FSB arrests German national accused of serving as Ukrainian mercenary sniper
content: Russian Federal Security Service agents have detained a German citizen, accusing him of serving as a mercenary sniper for Ukraine’s armed forces. The FSB says he deserted after allegedly not receiving pay and notes that he previously served as a sniper in Germany’s Bundeswehr.
summary: Russian FSB agents arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They said he deserted over unpaid wages and had previously served as a sniper in the Bundeswehr.
author: DW World

title: EU regulators investigate Booking.com over fake listings and phishing scams
content: European Commission calls accommodation website’s approach to fraudulent listings and phishing scams as ‘absolutely substandard’ EU regulators have opened an investigation into Booking. Com, alleging that the accommodation website has not done enough to protect consumers from fake listings and scams. The European Commission, which regulates the world’s biggest tech companies operating in the EU, said Booking. Com may have breached the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA) with its “absolutely substandard” approach to tackling fraudulent listings and phishing scams, where criminals impersonate a third party to trick people to hand over money.
summary: EU regulators investigate Booking.com over fake listings and phishing scams.
author: Guardian World

title: Poland's parliament approves bills easing abortion ban, faces likely presidential veto
content:
Poland’s lower house of parliament approved two bills that would loosen the country’s near‑total abortion ban.  Campaigners describe the move as a “small‑scale step” and say it comes amid protests demanding the government follow through on promises to overhaul abortion laws.

The new measures would remove some criminal penalties for people who help women access abortion care and would allow terminations in cases of fetal abnormalities.  Officials say the bills are likely to be vetoed by President Jarosław Kaczyński.
summary: Poland’s lower house of parliament approved two bills to loosen the near‑total abortion ban. The measures would cut penalties for those helping women obtain abortions and allow terminations for fetal abnormalities, but are expected to be vetoed by the nationalist president.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian MPs fund personal security upgrades after alleged attack on Helen Haines
content:
Australian federal politicians have said they are spending thousands of dollars on personal security upgrades as concerns grow over widening threats. The statements follow safety briefings by the Australian Federal Police and ASIO after an alleged attack on MP Helen Haines, who lost both legs in the incident on Monday.

In response, security agencies said they will review safety precautions for MPs’ homes and offices. The Labor government and other parliamentarians are considering options for when they return to Canberra next week, including establishing a new committee on MPs’ safety, allocating greater resources to police and moving motions of condolence for Haines.

Crossbench members have renewed calls for reforms to question time and the tone of parliamentary debate, though the major parties are not expected to adopt those proposals.
summary: Australian MPs fund personal security upgrades after alleged attack on Helen Haines.
author: Guardian World

title: Shark named Bukang-i freed after month trapped in Busan canal
content: Bukang-i successfully guided out after month in which it drew 1.6m visitors and was watched over by YouTubers In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch. Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affectionately known as Bukang-i. On Wednesday, after more than a month in the canal and at the third attempt, the shark was successfully guided out, South Korea’s oceans ministry said. Officials expect her to move into open water in time.
summary: South Korea’s oceans ministry said the shark, affectionately known as Bukang-i, was successfully guided out of the Busan canal after more than a month trapped. During its confinement the shark drew 1.6 million visitors and was monitored nightly by local volunteers in hi‑vis vests and by YouTubers.
author: Guardian World

title: Taiwan charges five men in plot to ram car into comedian over Xi jokes
content:
Taiwanese prosecutors in New Taipei have charged five men with a plot to ram a car into comedian Huang Yi‑hao, who had mocked the Chinese Communist Party and Xi Jinping. According to the indictment, a person identified only as “K” from China paid the defendants to carry out the attack.

The case is cited by Taipei as part of a pattern of alleged transnational repression by Beijing, which the island accuses of trying to silence critics despite its claim over the territory.
summary: Taiwanese prosecutors have charged five men in a plot to ram a car into comedian Huang Yi-hao. Prosecutors say a person identified as ‘K’ from China paid the five defendants to injure Huang, who mocked the Chinese Communist Party and Xi Jinping.
author: Guardian World

title: Gravely ill ICE detainees in Florida set for deportation to unknown African countries
content:
Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails claim that U.S. authorities are preparing to deport their loved ones to unknown African countries, even though the detainees’ medical conditions are worsening. According to the families and the immigration‑advocacy group Workers Circle, flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled to depart as early as Wednesday.

Workers Circle has been monitoring conditions inside the two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida and has spoken with the detainees. The group reports that the scheduled flights represent an imminent transfer of the severely ill detainees to destinations in Africa that are not specified.
summary: Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two ICE facilities in south Florida say authorities plan to deport them to unknown African countries. Flights to third‑country destinations with no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the advocacy group the Workers Circle.
author: Guardian World

title: US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in Guinea-Bissau newborns halted
content: Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’ The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday. It is “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”
summary: The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns in Guinea-Bissau was halted. Lead researcher Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer said the study will not move forward because the necessary governmental approval was not given.
author: Guardian World

title: Family of prison officer killed by IRA receives state apology
content: The family of prison officer Brian Stack, who was shot in the back of the neck while crossing a street in Dublin in 1983 and died 18 months later, has received a state apology. The apology addresses the death of Stack at the hands of the IRA.
summary: The state apologized to the family of prison officer Brian Stack, who was killed by the IRA. Stack was shot in the back of the neck while crossing a street in Dublin in 1983 and died 18 months later.
author: BBC World

title: New book details 1949 meeting between Langston Hughes and Nina Simone
content: A new book charts how a 1949 meeting between the renowned poet and the legendary musician, then a 16-year-old girl, sparked enduring ties and fruitful collaboration In 1949, the poet and writer Langston Hughes was already a towering figure – he toured the country reading his poems and lecturing, drawing crowds that filled auditoriums. That year, at a lecture in Asheville, North Carolina, Hughes met a 16-year-old girl, Eunice Waymon, who would go on to make history in her own right using her stage name, Nina Simone. Hughes and Simone became friends and collaborators, working together on songs such as Backlash Blues, which soundtracked what was then a nascent Black Power movement. The song influenced Kwame Ture, the activist and Black revolutionary who was then known as Stokely Carmichael, who popularized the phrase “Black power”.
summary: A new book charts how a 1949 meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, between poet Langston Hughes and 16-year-old Eunice Waymon sparked an enduring friendship. The two collaborated on songs such as Backlash Blues, which influenced activist Stokely Carmichael.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Thure Erik Lund's 'The Mystery of What Befell in the Ditch' translated into English
content: Translated into English at last, this portrait of a man appalled by modernity and desperate to get back to nature is brimming with Nordic weltschmerz T-O-M. The initials of Tomas Olsen Myrbråten, the narrator in Thure Erik Lund’s The Mystery of What Befell in the Ditch, spell out the Norwegian word for “empty”. Approaching 38, he’s already a relic. He spends his days slumped at the kitchen table or staring out of the window, convinced that the ceiling is about to fall and crush him. He sobs about the state he’s in and the state of society around him. Of one thing he’s sure: “It is no longer me who cries, but the world, the world crying, in me.” Nordic weltschmerz: you’d have to be a saint not to giggle. Lund has been described by Karl Ove Knausgård as the “greatest Norwegian contemporary writer”; this novel, originally published in 1999, is his first to be translated into English. In it, Tomas describes himself, over and over and over again, as a “life-of-the-mind individual”. Cursed as much as blessed, life-of-the mind individuals have a keen and unconsoling sense of how things are (“one is a wretched, contemptible, and unworthy being”) and how things will end for them (“in the sewers of society, at nature’s nadir, incessantly ground down into the mud and the mire so that one day, millions of years from now, they become oil, life-of-the-mind oil, at the very bottom of life itself”). Is he making fun of himself? In 2026, he seems closer to an eco-prophet.
summary: This novel, originally published in 1999, is the first work by Thure Erik Lund to be translated into English. The book features a narrator named Tomas Olsen Myrbråten who is described as a "life-of-the-mind individual" appalled by modernity.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Coach banned until 2048 for training DR Congo kids while suspended for sexual abuse
content:
Jonathan Bukabakwa, a coach in the Democratic Republic of the Congo known as Messi, has had his Fifa ban extended by five years until 2048. The world governing body imposed the additional penalty after the Guardian revealed that Bukabakwa continued to train young players despite being suspended for the sexual abuse of a minor. He had previously received a 20-year ban from football.

In addition to the extended ban, Bukabakwa was ordered to pay a $15,000 (£11,200) fine. The DRC’s Football Association was also ordered to improve its education and compliance measures.
summary: Coach banned until 2048 for training DR Congo kids while suspended for sexual abuse.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to have surgery after ACL rupture, PSG's most serious injury
content:
Paris Saint-Germain’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during Tuesday’s 4-2 Champions League victory over Barcelona. The Georgian player twisted his knee just before the hour mark and was helped off the pitch, unable to put any weight on his right leg.

This injury is the most serious of three sustained by PSG, as Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos are also out for weeks.
summary: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during Paris Saint‑Germain’s 4‑2 Champions League win over Barcelona. His injury is the most serious of three PSG injuries, with Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos also out for weeks.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Gary Neville's The Overlap goes daily as Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart join
content:
Gary Neville’s podcast, The Overlap, has transitioned to a daily format, reflecting the creator’s expanding media presence. Recent additions to the show include former footballers Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart, joining a growing roster of guests. This expansion occurs against a backdrop where former footballers are increasingly entering the creator economy, with many establishing podcasts or YouTube channels.

The article notes that while other former players like Gary Lineker have diversified their content, The Overlap largely remains focused on football. Although a rugby podcast associated with the brand was discontinued in February, a cricket equivalent continues to operate. The piece positions Neville’s media empire as a dominant force in this sector, distinguishing it from the broader, more varied agenda of rival productions.
summary: The Overlap has transitioned to a daily format with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to the podcast family. The content primarily focuses on football, while a rugby podcast was mothballed in February and a cricket equivalent continues.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Philipp Lahm: Manchester City's rule-breaking deserves punishment
content: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri.
summary: Philipp Lahm states that while Manchester City achieved greatness, their rule-breaking behavior deserves to be punished. He also notes that the Bundesliga's member-controlled structure can show the way forward for football.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Chris Woakes publishes autobiography The Wizard
content: All-rounder and ‘the best teammate you could wish for’ has seen profound change since his first-class debut in 2006 The Spin this week comes from York, where Chris Woakes and I sat down on Monday evening to discuss his new autobiography, The Wizard. There were just shy of 400 international wickets on stage, not a single one mine, and an audience that happened to include one of his old teachers. It turns out a seemingly clean-cut cricketer was something of a rebel back in the day, with Mr Wager reminding Chris of the time he feigned illness to bunk off school for a long weekend in Newquay with his mates. A bit like Warwickshire’s title win this year that anecdote came too late, frustratingly, for the hardback edition.
summary: Chris Woakes released his new autobiography, The Wizard, and discussed it in York. The book details his life as an all-rounder and teammate since his first-class debut in 2006.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Antonelli's first F1 title and Mercedes upgrades in focus at Austin GP
content:
Kimi Antonelli is poised to secure his maiden Formula 1 world championship at the United States Grand Prix in Austin this weekend. The young Italian driver’s title is described as all but secured, marking the culmination of a childhood dream. The event is expected to bring intense media attention as Antonelli attempts to seal his first championship.

While the driver’s primary focus is on winning the title, his Mercedes team faces significant scrutiny regarding performance. The outcome at the United States Grand Prix will provide crucial insights into Mercedes’ upgrades, which will inform the team’s strategy and competitiveness as they prepare for next season’s championship run.
summary: Kimi Antonelli is poised to secure his maiden championship at the United States Grand Prix in Austin. Mercedes will also use the event to assess performance upgrades that will inform their strategy for next season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jonas Eidevall says San Diego Wave eye title as they sit second in NWSL
content: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is reveling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the NWSL, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.”
summary: Former Arsenal head coach Jonas Eidevall leads San Diego Wave, who are second in the NWSL, one point behind the leader with two matches before the playoffs. The team is on a five‑game winning streak and Eidevall says they can go all the way and are targeting silverware.

title: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield, bringing relief to Aberdeen workers
content:
The UK has approved the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, a decision that has brought relief to Aberdeen despite limited expectations for a return to past economic highs. While few believe the approval will restore the city to its previous boom years, local workers hope it will secure North Sea jobs for the time being. The development is seen as a stabilizing factor for the region’s economy, with some residents noting that the project helps them pay their mortgages.

Aberdeen’s current economic landscape contrasts sharply with its history. In 2012, the city boasted the highest concentration of millionaires in the UK, a status bolstered by an ATM reportedly having the highest withdrawal rate in Europe during the 1990s. During that era, fossil fuel firms transformed the city’s grand granite houses into company offices, and house prices skyrocketed as workers scrambled for space.

However, the city has experienced a significant reversal since the 2014 oil price shock. Today, “for sale” and “to let” signs are common on Aberdeen’s main thoroughfares. Disposable income in the city has fallen by nearly 20% between 2013 and 2023, a decline that is more severe than in any other large UK city.
summary: The UK has approved the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, providing relief for workers hoping to secure local employment. Although few believe the decision will restore Aberdeen’s past boom years, the city has experienced a significant decline in disposable income since 2013.

title: 12-mile tunnel proposed to solve Windermere sewage pollution
content:
United Utilities, the Environment Agency, and local campaigners have announced plans for a 12-mile tunnel designed to transport sewage away from Windermere, England’s largest lake. The project aims to address widespread raw sewage and bacterial pollution in the Lake District, which is driven by discharges from United Utilities.

Campaigners state that this pollution has led to more frequent toxic blue-green algal blooms. Consequently, the public has been advised to avoid swimming in the lake.
summary: United Utilities, the Environment Agency, and local campaigners are planning a 12-mile tunnel to transport sewage away from Windermere. The lake has experienced raw sewage discharges and toxic algal blooms that have led to swimming advisories.

title: US extreme weather survivors organize into political force
content:
A growing number of US residents affected by extreme weather disasters are organizing into a political force. At a recent gathering in Texas, near the site of last year’s floods that killed 136 people, survivors united on the need for urgent action. Estimates suggest that severe wildfires, floods, storms, and other calamities now impact about half of all Americans as the climate crisis intensifies these events.

These survivors are coalescing to advocate for improved disaster response. Additionally, some are pushing for action on the politically contentious issue of global heating.
summary: Survivors of US extreme weather disasters are organizing into a political force to demand improved disaster response and action on global heating. This movement is growing as severe climate-related events now affect about half of all Americans.

title: Mayer Hillman, Pioneer of Climate Crisis and Road Safety Ideas, Dies
content:
Mayer Hillman, a social scientist and author, has passed away, leaving behind a legacy as a pioneer in climate crisis and road safety ideas. He was also a dedicated champion of walking, cycling, and children’s mobility. In the late 1990s, Hillman predicted that future generations would question the actions taken by their predecessors to prevent global climate catastrophe. This foresight was echoed two decades later when Greta Thunberg addressed the United Nations, stating that young people were beginning to understand the betrayal of the current generation and that the eyes of future generations were upon them.

Additionally, Hillman warned twenty-five years ago that public denial of the climate crisis would only begin to crack when people in the global north were personally affected. He cited specific scenarios for this shift, including the creation of millions of environmental refugees from uninhabitable regions or instances where homes were flooded repeatedly, making them uninsurable. His work highlighted the connection between direct personal impact and the breakdown of public denial regarding environmental issues.
summary: Mayer Hillman, a social scientist and author, pioneered ideas linking climate crisis, road safety, and children’s mobility. He warned that denial of climate change would break only when people in the global north faced environmental refugees and repeated flooding, prompting future generations to demand action.

title: Chlamydomonas alga and channelrhodopsin illuminate brain memory mechanisms
content:
A one‑celled alga called Chlamydomonas has contributed to research that earned three scientists the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine this month. The study shows how memories, feelings and behaviour form in the brain, using the alga’s light‑sensing protein as a model.

Chlamydomonas swims toward light by means of a protein named channelrhodopsin. This protein is remarkably similar to the rhodopsin found in human eyes.

When channelrhodopsin detects light, electrically charged ions rush into the cell from outside. The influx triggers an extremely fast electrical signal that directs the alga’s hair‑like motor to move.
summary: Researchers used the one-celled alga Chlamydomonas, which swims toward light via the protein channelrhodopsin, to study how memories, feelings and behaviour form in the brain. When channelrhodopsin detects light, ions rush into the cell, triggering a rapid electrical signal that directs the alga's hair-like motor to move.

title: Vision Zero Network Founder Advocates for Reducing Traffic Deaths
content:
Traffic crashes kill more than one million people annually, serving as the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the United States, 100 people lose their lives to traffic incidents daily, with many fatalities occurring on rural and local streets rather than highways. Leah Shahum, founder and director of the Vision Zero Network, a nonprofit dedicated to reducing street fatalities, notes that while traffic deaths are a leading cause of preventable death, they are often treated as inevitable.

The causes of these crashes involve both driver errors, such as speeding and distraction, and infrastructure failures, including roads designed for speed rather than safety. Laura Sandt of the University of North Carolina Highway Safety Research Center describes the situation as having many moving parts, which creates numerous opportunities for injury prevention. However, implementation is often hindered by government red tape, despite the availability of cheap, proven traffic-calming measures like lowering speed limits and using planters to tighten intersections.

Despite a historical decline in the US traffic death rate from a 1930s peak of 30.8 per 100,000 people, the past decade has seen a rise in deadly pedestrian incidents. Communities are increasingly recognizing the importance of traffic safety policy. Hoboken, New Jersey, has recorded no traffic fatalities since 2017 due to increased public transit investment, extended curbs to promote walkability, and the use of cameras to identify intersections needing redesign. Greg Francese, the city’s acting director of transportation and parking, acknowledges that proving an intersection is deadly is necessary to justify changes like removing parking spaces.

While Hoboken’s success may not directly translate to larger, car-centric cities, other examples demonstrate feasibility. Edmonton, Alberta, a city of around one million people, reduced traffic fatalities by 63% and serious injuries by 40% between 2015 and 2020 by adjusting speed limits and improving crosswalk signals. The primary challenge remains securing the funding and political will to implement these known technical adjustments.
summary: Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the US, 100 people a day lose their lives this way, in many cases not on highways but on rural and local streets.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Researchers achieve 90% PFAS destruction with electrochemical method
content: Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a. K. A. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond between carbon and fluorine, which the environment struggles to break down. The sticking points PFAS are everywhere: They spew from factories and slough off products and into water with normal use. Scientists have found them in everything from human blood to Antarctic snow. One 2022 report found that 89% of the US population had PFAS in excess of two nanograms per milliliter of blood plasma, a common threshold for potential adverse health effects, and 9% of the population had passed the riskier level of 20 nanograms per milliliter. The PFAS monster is also a moving target. New compounds are still being created and used. There are more than 12,000 of them, and much of the cleanup research focuses on only a small handful. The progress Cleansing PFAS-contaminated soil is a project in its infancy, but it is possible to prevent more buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems. There are two ways to handle this: trap or destroy. Some scientists have found reverse osmosis—a process that pushes water through supertight filters—useful in point-of-use cases, like water filters at kitchen sinks. Other techniques in the pipeline might be more suitable for large-scale removal—for example, at water treatment facilities. One, called foam fractionation, generates bubbles that capture PFAS. More approaches, like ensnaring the chemicals in nanothin layers of charged metal, are also under investigation. Trapping, though, is imperfect. You’re left with PFAS-filled brine, which if not properly destroyed (an expensive and energy-sucking endeavor) can still end up in the environment. Jack Huang, a professor of crop and soil sciences at the University of Georgia, is working on destruction. He’s testing a method called electrochemical degradation, which uses electrodes to break down the bonds that hold PFAS together. The product destroyed more than 90% of PFAS mass in tests and has already been licensed by the engineering consulting firm AECOM. Ridding life of PFAS is also a policy challenge. There are alternatives; we just need the push to use them. And we’ve had success before: The EPA’s 2010/2015 PFOA Stewardship Program has helped slash the release of water-repellent perfluorooctanoic acid by 95%. More recently, Minnesota, Maine, and New Mexico have passed bans on PFAS in products like cookware and dental floss. Progress meter ………… 6 Scientists are making strides toward removing and destroying PFAS—but it’ll be all for naught if we don’t turn off the tap.
summary: Researchers achieve 90% PFAS destruction with electrochemical method.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Researchers develop drugs to mimic exercise benefits for those with disabilities
content:
Researchers are investigating how to translate the physiological benefits of exercise into pharmaceutical treatments for individuals with frailty, disability, or chronic illness. While the goal is not to replace physical activity, scientists aim to replicate specific health perks, such as muscle building, bone strengthening, and mood improvement. This endeavor requires identifying the complex cascade of hormones, enzymes, and molecules triggered by movement, a process that remains in its early stages.

Developing safe and effective drugs presents significant challenges, as more than 90% of treatments entering human studies fail. Additionally, regulatory barriers exist because the FDA approves medications for treating diseases rather than enhancing general wellness. Thomas Burris, a pharmacologist at the University of Florida, notes that his work focuses on conditions that respond to exercise, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, and dementia.

Despite these hurdles, progress has been made in identifying exercise-related signals and developing compounds to regulate them. Burris’s lab has designed a drug that increases the activity of a specific receptor in muscle cells, which is normally active but boosted by working out. In mouse studies, animals treated with this drug ran longer and farther than untreated mice, effectively becoming “marathon mice” without exercise. The compound also showed indications of mimicking cognitive benefits and potentially helping treat heart failure in mice. Burris founded a company called Pelagos to advance this work toward clinical trials.

Other medications mimicking exercise effects have also entered human studies. In June, biotech firm Cambrian Bio reported that its experimental drug ATX-304 increased metabolism and reduced liver and belly fat in people with obesity and prediabetes. The drug activates a metabolic switch that helps cells sense low energy supplies, a mechanism similar to that used during sustained physical activity. Cambrian aims to help patients lose weight without losing muscle, addressing a common concern associated with GLP-1 medicines.
summary: Scientists are developing medicines to replicate the health benefits of physical activity for people with frailty, disability, or chronic illness. While Thomas Burris’s lab found a compound that improved endurance in mice, other firms like Cambrian Bio have entered human trials for drugs that boost metabolism.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: NASA Plans Nuclear-Powered Spacecraft SR-1 to Reach Mars by 2029
content:
NASA has announced plans to construct Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1), the first nuclear-reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft. The agency intends to launch an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, with the craft arriving in 2029. This initiative follows the Artemis II crew’s lunar slingshot mission in April. A successful deployment would mark a new era in spaceflight, potentially reducing travel times and limiting astronaut exposure to cosmic radiation. Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales, described the announcement as a significant positive development.

While the concept is not new, with the Soviet Union having previously launched dozens of reactors for spy satellites, US development has been marked by delays. Over the past 75 years, the US has initiated and terminated several related programs. The most recent, DRACO, a collaboration between NASA and the Department of Defense, was canceled in 2025 due to high experimentation costs, price competitiveness issues compared to conventional rockets, and safety concerns regarding ground tests. Despite these historical setbacks, Philip Metzger, a spaceflight engineering researcher at the Florida Space Institute, characterized the technology as very doable.

NASA is currently pursuing a $2 billion investment in nuclear electric propulsion. This system utilizes neutrons from a self-sustaining uranium-fission reaction to generate heat and electricity. The electricity ionizes a gas, which is expelled via magnetic fields to create thrust. Sebastian Corbisiero, the US Department of Energy’s national technical director of space reactor programs, noted that while the thrust is low, the efficiency allows for long-duration operation. Steve Sinacore, program director of NASA’s SR-1 program, presented a design resembling a fletched arrow, with the power system at the rear and a uranium-filled reactor at the tip.

The reactor is designed with a capacity of at least 20 kilowatts, which is significantly less powerful than a typical Earth-based nuclear plant. Large fins on the spacecraft will radiate heat into space to cool the reactor. Safety protocols require the reactor to be switched on approximately two days after launch, once the spacecraft is sufficiently distant from Earth, to manage the dangerous waste products generated during operation. Middleburgh highlighted the challenge of surviving the launch vibrations, describing the experience as being shaken, rattled, and rolled.

Idaho National Laboratory is currently building the reactor, with NASA stating that procurement of major components is underway and integration work is advancing steadily. The agency remains on target for a late-2028 launch. Lindsey Holmes, vice president of advanced projects at Analytical Mechanics Associates, called the timeline aggressive, suggesting that the push may be influenced by the deep-space nuclear ambitions of China and Russia. These two nations have discussed plans to place a reactor on the lunar surface in the mid-2030s to power a jointly operated base. Regardless of SR-1’s outcome, the development is expected to facilitate NASA’s own efforts to place a reactor on the moon, as both environments involve a vacuum.
summary: NASA announced the Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1), a nuclear-reactor-powered spacecraft that will carry an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028 and arrive in 2029. The project, worth $2 billion, will use a 20 kW uranium reactor and is being built at Idaho National Laboratory with a planned launch in late 2028.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: MIT Technology Review print editor launches audacious new issue
content:
The new editor of MIT Technology Review’s print magazine has introduced a thematic focus for the current issue, centering on “impossible ideas.” In a personal introduction, the editor explains that the publication is taking a more audacious approach, encouraging experimentation and playfulness in its content. This shift is part of a broader effort to balance practical journalism with ambitious storytelling, a dynamic the editor describes as a constant tension between ambition and reality throughout their twenty-plus-year career as a science and tech journalist.

The editor notes that recent issues have seen the return of regular rosters of lists and infographics, elements that the magazine handles effectively. However, the most significant change is the current issue’s dedication to exploring concepts that may seem unattainable. The editor, who joined the team this past spring, was invited by editor in chief Mat Honan to explain this new direction. The goal is to provide readers with a slate of stories that examine ideas often considered impractical or overly optimistic.

The rationale for this focus includes the enjoyment of dreaming about scenarios such as living on the moon or uploading human brains. The editor argues that maintaining a sense of ambition is difficult when addressing the world’s problems feels like playing whack-a-mole. Furthermore, the issue highlights scientists and engineers who continue to pursue daring endeavors, such as creating synthetic blood or decoding animal speech. These efforts serve as a reminder of technology’s intended purpose: to apply cutting-edge research to make life better, safer, healthier, and more joyful.

The introduction also addresses the necessity of correcting technological failures. The editor points to issues like forever chemicals, traffic deaths, and AI that encourages dangerous user behavior as examples of when technology has made things worse. In such cases, the responsibility is to assess the damage and find ways to fix what has been broken, even when the task of unraveling the mess seems impossible.

Prior to joining MIT Technology Review, the editor spent three years editing a newsletter focused on individual actions to address the climate crisis. Although some critics have labeled such individual efforts a fool’s errand due to the scale of the problem, the editor found that focusing on limitations only deepens the sense of hopelessness. The issue is dedicated to individuals who possess the audacity to try and refuse to let themselves or others say no, aiming to inspire readers to engage with these challenging concepts.
summary: The new issue of MIT Technology Review, edited by a 20‑plus‑year science journalist, focuses on impossible ideas for the end of 2026. The editor, who joined the magazine this spring, says the goal is to experiment audaciously and inspire ambition.
author: MIT Tech Review

content: Lili Infante, a former Russian child who fled a chaotic upbringing, rose to become a standout law‑enforcement professional in the United States. She pioneered the DEA’s investigations into the dark web, working on crypto‑related cases without realizing the identities she would uncover.

title: PHP releases critical patch to fix two severe vulnerabilities
content:
Security patches for the PHP programming language, widely used to build websites and web apps, are scheduled to be released today. The updates aim to address two critical vulnerabilities that could cause significant disruption across the internet if left unpatched.

According to an advisory issued on Tuesday, the PHP developers rated the vulnerabilities at 9.2 out of 10 on the severity scale. Some cybersecurity agencies have advised website operators to take their systems offline temporarily if they cannot apply the fix immediately.

The patch is expected to become available at 10 AM ET today, with developers noting they may release it earlier if the vulnerability details allow.
summary: PHP developers are releasing a security patch today at 10AM ET to fix two critical vulnerabilities. The vulnerabilities carry a severity rating of 9.2, and cybersecurity agencies are urging sites that cannot apply the patch immediately to temporarily take their systems offline.
author: The Verge

title: iPhone Duo deemed risky, messy first‑gen Apple product that may please early adopters
content:
The iPhone Duo is described as Apple’s riskiest product in recent years, representing a major rethink of what an iPhone could be.  It carries the seeds of several intriguing ideas that might prove valuable in future releases, though those possibilities have not yet materialized.

According to the report, the Duo is one of Apple’s messiest first‑generation releases in a long time.  It is expected to excite gadget enthusiasts and early adopters while likely frustrating the broader user base.  The piece notes that the last significant change to the iPhone’s design was the iPhone X, which removed the home button nearly a decade ago and was considered a relatively subtle improvement.
summary: The iPhone Duo is described as the riskiest Apple product in years and a messy first‑generation device that represents a huge rethink of the iPhone. It is expected to delight gadget nerds and early adopters while likely frustrating most other users.
author: The Verge

title: Reviewer praises iPhone Duo's matte inner display as its best feature
content:
The iPhone Duo is described as a first‑generation product that still carries some of the messiness typical of early foldable releases. Despite design choices that the reviewer does not fully endorse, the phone’s 7.6‑inch inner display stands out because of its matte, nano‑texture finish.

The reviewer has been using the Duo for a week, watching movies on a plane, browsing a photo gallery, and reading. During that time, the matte screen’s performance convinced the reviewer that it is the device’s best feature.

Having tried a dozen or so book‑style foldables over the past five years, the reviewer notes that every other inner screen has lacked the same finish. The reviewer hopes that other foldable makers will adopt a similar matte, nano‑textured display.
summary: The reviewer says the matte nano‑texture finish on the iPhone Duo’s 7.6‑inch inner screen is the device’s best feature. They have used the screen for movies, photos and reading on a plane and hope other foldable makers will adopt the finish.
author: The Verge

title: Spotify launches first native Android Automotive car app in select Audi models
content:
Spotify announced Wednesday that it is releasing a next‑generation, fully native in‑car app built on Google’s Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which begins rolling out today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle’s infotainment hardware, removing the need for phone tethering, Bluetooth connections or auxiliary cables.

The company said the launch signals a shift away from reliance on Apple CarPlay and Android phone‑projection systems that currently dominate in‑car media consumption.
summary: Spotify announced Wednesday that it is releasing a fully native in‑car app built on Google’s Android Automotive operating system. The app is debuting today in select Audi vehicles and runs directly on the car’s infotainment hardware, removing the need for phone tethering, Bluetooth or aux cables.
author: The Verge

title: Top gifts for nine-year-olds chosen by kids and parents
content: Popcorn makers, Lego Fortnite and the coolest water bottle around … surprise the mini tween in your life with our pick of the top gifts and toys • The best gifts for eight-year-olds The start of the tween years, nine years old, is a sweet spot between curiosity and growing independence, making it a fun, though sometimes tricky, age to buy for. Kids at this age are up for a challenge, whether that means trying a trickier craft set, playing a more complex game or stepping up their sporting interests. Pitch a gift right and you’ll not only get the whoop of joy when they first receive it, but something that will hold their interest and help them develop their skills, interests and hobbies over time.
summary: The guide recommends items such as popcorn makers, a Lego Fortnite set and a popular water bottle as top gifts for nine‑year‑olds. It notes that nine‑year‑olds are at a sweet spot between curiosity and growing independence, enjoying more challenging crafts, games and sports.

title: UK watchdogs urged to act after 14‑year‑old's suicide linked to TikTok content
content: Adriana Retyte took her own life after viewing ‘high-risk’ material on the video-sharing platform TikTok A 14-year-old schoolgirl’s death after TikTok served her suicide content has prompted renewed calls for UK watchdogs to crack down on “toxic” social media feeds. Adriana Retyte, a pupil at Langley school in Norfolk, took her own life after she viewed videos and images related to suicide on the video-sharing platform, according to a coroner who last week found her access to the material on TikTok “may have played a significant part in her decision to take her life”.
summary: Adriana Retyte, a 14‑year‑old pupil at Langley school in Norfolk, took her own life after viewing suicide‑related videos and images on TikTok. A coroner said her access to the material may have played a significant part and called for UK watchdogs to crack down on “toxic” social media feeds.

summary: Wildfires have blanketed Palangkaraya on the Indonesian island of Borneo in toxic haze for weeks. Residents are struggling with persistent coughs, falling incomes and disrupted education.

content: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he will order a “massive” police deployment for the new demonstrations that the Yellow Vest movement has called for on Saturday. In a parliamentary session marked by angry lawmakers, Lecornu admitted the previous security response was insufficient and pledged a stronger approach for the upcoming protests.

title: Egypt considers joining Saudi Arabia in war against Houthis
content:
Egypt is considering entering the conflict against the Houthi movement, according to a report by Camille Corcoran. The Saudi kingdom has faced sustained Houthi attacks since a Yemeni truce collapsed in September, prompting Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to travel to Egypt in mid‑September to request possible military assistance.

The Egyptian president placed the request before parliament on Saturday, indicating that a formal decision on participation may be forthcoming.
summary: Egypt is weighing participation in Saudi Arabia's war against the Iran‑backed Houthi rebels. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman visited Egypt in mid‑September to request military support, and the Egyptian president placed the request before parliament on Saturday.

title: US envoy Steve Witkoff meets Putin in St. Petersburg to discuss Ukraine invasion
content:
US envoy Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss Moscow’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine. The talks occurred while US President Donald Trump is urging Kyiv to reach a deal that would end the fighting.

The day before the St. Petersburg meeting, Witkoff had spoken with Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo, Norway. The report was provided by France 24 international affairs editor Philip Turle.
summary: US envoy Steve Witkoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday about Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The day before, the American official had met with Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo, Norway.

title: US envoy Steve Witkoff thanks Putin for diesel deal during Ukraine talks in Russia
content: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg, where he thanked the Russian leader for a diesel deal discussed during the Ukraine talks. The face‑to‑face meeting followed Witkoff’s earlier discussions with Ukraine’s president and other European leaders in Oslo. title: Macron calls world leaders' remarks on France riots 'stupid' and based on fake AI videos
content: French President Emmanuel Macron criticised several world leaders, naming U.S. President Donald Trump, for making “stupid” remarks about the riots and looting that accompanied peaceful protests in France on Saturday, saying they were based on fabricated AI videos and used for political gain. He noted that another wave of demonstrations over the country’s rising cost of living is scheduled for the upcoming Saturday.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.

title: MPs warn civil service pension delays could trigger tax bills for bereaved families
content: MPs have warned that “chaos” at the civil service pension scheme, which is run by Capita, may cause some lump‑sum payments to miss the two‑year deadline that keeps them tax‑free. The delay could mean bereaved families receive “unconscionable” tax bills because the tax‑free status applies only if the scheme is notified of a member’s death and makes the payment within two years. The government has been alerted to the risk that the scheme’s problems could lead to unjust tax charges for surviving relatives.
summary: MPs say chaos at the Capita‑run civil service pension scheme could cause some lump‑sum payments to miss the two‑year tax‑free deadline. As a result, bereaved families could face tax bills on those payments, which the government has been warned are unconscionable.
