title: Burnham and Badenoch clash over Jackdaw gasfield decision as supply begins
content:
The UK government announced that the Jackdaw gasfield will begin supplying gas to homes and businesses from the end of the month. An explainer on the decision was provided by Jill Ambrose. Environmental groups have condemned the move, with Ami McCarthy, head of politics for Greenpeace UK, saying that approving Jackdaw shows the toxic grip fossil‑fuel lobbyists still hold over energy policy.

Andy Burnham promised pragmatism in the debate, but critics argue that the project will not lower energy bills, boost security, or create many jobs. They point out that Jackdaw will provide only about 27 full‑time positions, will not reduce Britain’s reliance on expensive oil and gas, and will leave households financially strained.

Shell is expected to cheer the decision, yet it will not cut bills or make a meaningful difference to the gas supply. Jackdaw is projected to supply roughly 2 % of the country’s gas demand for about ten years, is largely unmanned and operated remotely, and will not stop the decline in North Sea jobs.
summary: The Jackdaw field will start supplying gas to homes and businesses from the end of the month, the government said Here is an explainer by Jill Ambrose about the Jackdaw decision. But environmental groups have condemned the decision.
author: Guardian World

title: Europe sees surge of protests over schools, housing and shortages in multiple capitals
content:
Protests are sweeping several European capitals as citizens voice anger over public‑service failures. In France, piles of wheelie bins placed at school entrances signaled student frustration with deteriorating classrooms and teacher shortages. Spain’s capital saw a growing tent camp where residents demonstrated against soaring housing costs. Similar demonstrations have emerged in Belgium, Italy and Portugal, while clashes erupted in Tirana, Albania, suggesting an autumn of unrest across the region.

According to the report, governments appear hamstrung and lack answers to these furious demands, raising the likelihood of further discontent throughout Europe.
summary: Protests have erupted in France, Spain, Belgium, Italy, Portugal and Albania over issues such as crumbling classrooms, teacher shortages and soaring housing costs. Demonstrators have placed wheelie bins at school entrances, set up a tent camp in the capital and clashed in Tirana, while governments appear unable to meet the demands, suggesting further discontent.
author: Guardian World

title: Guardian live Q&A on France riots with columnists Rokhaya Diallo, Alexander Hurst
content:
Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst will go live at 3 pm BST / 4 pm CEST on Friday 23 October to answer reader questions about the recent riots and protests in France. Readers can submit questions by email to conversations@theguardian.com or join the discussion later that day.

The riots followed weeks of protests that saw a town hall set ablaze, more than 2,000 shops looted, 2,300 arrests and around 1,000 police injured. Allegations of police brutality emerged, and the unrest unsettled investors, prompting a debt sell‑off that pushed borrowing costs above those of Greece. With a presidential election six months away, France’s national debt stands at 119 % of GDP—the highest since 1946—and its budget deficit is 5.1 %, among the EU’s highest, leaving “no money in the bank” to ease the cost‑of‑living squeeze that mobilised 550,000 demonstrators on Saturday, according to Guardian Europe correspondent Jon Henley.
summary: At 3pm BST / 4pm CEST Friday 23 Oct, Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst will be live taking questions from our readers about the riots and protests in France. Send your questions by email now to conversations@theguardian.
author: Guardian World

title: Putin orders release of Stephen Hubbard while meeting Trump envoy Steve Witkoff
content: Russia unilaterally frees Stephen Hubbard after US request while Steve Witkoff praises Putin as a ‘humanitarian’ Europe live – latest updates US politics live – latest updates Vladimir Putin ordered the release of an American from a Russian jail as he met Donald Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday for fresh talks on ending the war in Ukraine, amid increasingly close relations between Moscow and Washington. Trump had previously asked Putin to free Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old former teacher who had spent more than four years in Russian jails on charges of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine.
summary: Vladimir Putin ordered the release of Stephen Hubbard, a 74‑year‑old former teacher who had spent more than four years in Russian jail on mercenary‑warfare charges. The decision was announced as Putin met Donald Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg for talks on ending the war in Ukraine.

title: Macron calls other leaders' comments on French protests “unacceptable” and “stupid”
content: Macron says he is frustrated by the ‘visible manipulation of information’ about the events in France Meanwhile, back to Witkoff’s meeting with Putin in St Petersburg, the US president, Donald Trump, has just welcomed the release of Stephen Hubbard, a US citizen held by Moscow on allegations of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine ( 11:24 ). In a post on Truth Social, he said : “Stephen Hubbard, taken four years ago by Russia during the Biden Administration, was just released from prison, at the request of President Donald J. Trump, made directly to President Vladimir Putin in a telephone conversation last week. Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family. The United States, out of respect for President Trump, was not required to give anything in return - an unprecedented situation for Russia. There was no “swap” necessary for this release.
summary: Macron calls other leaders' comments on French protests “unacceptable” and “stupid”.

title: Independent MP Helen Haines loses both legs after alleged attack, stable condition
content:
Helen Haines, the independent MP for Indi, has lost both legs following an alleged targeted attack near her electorate office in north‑east Victoria. She remains in stable condition, and her husband says her heart and mind are in good shape.

Haines was struck by a car in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon and was in critical but stable condition. Surgeons attempted to save her right leg on Tuesday, but both legs had to be amputated because of the seriousness of her injuries.
summary: Independent MP Helen Haines is in stable condition after an alleged targeted attack near her north‑east Victoria electorate office that left her with both legs amputated. Surgeons attempted to save her right leg but both legs were removed due to the seriousness of her injuries.

title: Senator David Pocock proposes tax and transparency reforms in first press club speech
content: Independent senator’s goals ‘much bigger’ than prime ministership, he reveals in first speech to National Press Club Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast He’s six foot tall and full of muscle, but David Pocock’s real strength is often sounding like the most sensible, commonsense voice in the room. At his first speech to the National Press Club on Wednesday, he said he wasn’t launching a bid for prime minister – no matter how much some people might like the softly spoken senator to have more say in federal politics. A 25% tax on gas exports, which he said could fund anything from boosting welfare to health reforms and aged care. A 5% levy on datacentres to capture more benefits from the AI boom. Transparency reforms to shine a light on lobbyists, secret meetings with politicians and vested interests.
summary: Senator David Pocock proposes tax and transparency reforms in first press club speech.

title: Rams fall to Cardinals after losing kicker Blake Grupe in mid-game
content:
The Los Angeles Rams, initially projected as a Super Bowl contender following the assembly of a star-studded lineup, have struggled to maintain that status, currently sitting at a 2-4 record and last in the NFC West. The team has lost three of its last four games, with a recent defeat against the Arizona Cardinals marking a significant low point. In that matchup, the Cardinals, who had previously lost 16 of their last 19 meetings against Los Angeles, secured a victory without scoring a single touchdown.

Arizona’s kicker, Chad Ryland, drove the win by converting six field goal attempts, including a 43-yarder as time expired. The game highlighted a stark contrast in kicking performance, as the Rams were left without a kicker for the majority of the contest. Blake Grupe, acquired from the Jets practice squad, suffered an injury while covering a kickoff return in the first quarter. This left the team without a designated kicker after they had recently released Harrison Mevis, who had missed four kicks in the season’s first five weeks.
summary: The Los Angeles Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals on a field goal as time expired, dropping to a 2-4 record and last place in the NFC West. The Rams were left without a kicker for the remainder of the game after Blake Grupe was injured during a kickoff return.
author: Guardian Sport

title: PNG Chiefs unveil NRL jersey with Tabu art despite NZ Rugby naming dispute
content:
The PNG Chiefs have unveiled their logo and jersey ahead of their first NRL season in two years, proceeding despite an ongoing legal dispute with New Zealand Rugby over the use of the Chiefs name. A high court denied New Zealand Rugby's injunction regarding the moniker, allowing the team to move forward with their branding while the dispute remains pending.

The primary jersey features a black base with a white accented “V” and gold cultural drawings by PNG artist Tabu on the chest. The design also includes the face of a chief. An alternative version of the kit is available, which largely swaps the black color for white.
summary: The PNG Chiefs revealed their logo and jersey for their first NRL season while a legal dispute with New Zealand Rugby over the team name remains pending. The design features a black jersey with a white "V" and gold cultural drawings by PNG artist Tabu.

title: LeBron James leads Sixers to 106-100 win over Knicks in NBA opener
content:
The Philadelphia 76ers opened the NBA season with a 106‑100 victory over the New York Knicks, signaling their intent to compete for the title. The win came after the addition of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, who joined the team from Boston.

In the game, Tyrese Maxey led the squad with 28 points, while Brown contributed 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists in his first outing since being acquired. James, marking the start of his record‑setting 24th season, posted 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists. The result underscored the Sixers’ readiness to challenge the Knicks early in the campaign.
summary: LeBron James debuted with the Philadelphia 76ers as they defeated the New York Knicks 106-100, recording 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists. Tyrese Maxey scored 28 points and new acquisition Jaylen Brown added 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists.

title: IFR says it can force Manchester City owners to sell if verdict upheld
content:
David Kogan, chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), stated that the body possesses “absolute power” to compel Manchester City’s owners to sell the club if they are ultimately found to have managed it improperly. The IFR chair made these remarks as Manchester City continues to appeal against charges brought by the Premier League.

The club was previously found guilty by an independent commission of circumventing Premier League rules. The commission determined that Manchester City established “sham” commercial arrangements designed to inflate revenues or reduce costs by more than £900 million over a nine-season period.
summary: IFR says it can force Manchester City owners to sell if verdict upheld.

title: Ramaswamy Takes Responsibility for Attack Ad Targeting Amy Acton's Mother
content: Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy (R) confirmed to reporters Tuesday evening that his campaign produced a new attack ad featuring his Democratic opponent Amy Acton’s estranged mother. The ad, which began circulating on social media Monday night, includes the mother calling Acton a “liar” and insinuating she suffers from mental health issues. Ramaswamy acknowledged his campaign’s responsibility for the advertisement.
summary: Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy confirmed his campaign produced an attack ad featuring Amy Acton's mother. The ad called her a “liar”, insinuated she suffers from mental health issues, and began circulating on social media Monday night.

title: Los Angeles County officials find DOJ's 20,000 'likely' noncitizen voter list unreliable
content: Los Angeles County election officials stated that their preliminary analysis of a federal list identifying 20,000 "likely" noncitizens registered to vote in California indicates the list is "unreliable." The report notes that some individuals on this DOJ list appear to be U.S.-born.
summary: Election officials in Los Angeles County say their preliminary analysis of the federal government's list of 20,000 'likely' noncitizens registered to vote in California shows the list is 'unreliable.' The list was compiled by the Department of Justice.

title: UN urges 6% annual cuts to reverse 1.5°C overshoot by 2100
content: The United Nations has said the world must cut greenhouse gas emissions by nearly 6% per year to limit global warming enough to be able to return to the 1.5C goal by 2100, as decades of insufficient climate action have now made an overshoot inevitable. In a video message accompanying the UN Environment Programme’s (UNEP) 2026 Emissions Gap Report, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the world could no longer avoid overshooting the 1.5C limit and that the consequences were already devastating. However, he said it was still possible to return average global temperatures to 1.5C above preindustrial times by the end of the century. “Overshoot is not surrender,” he said, adding that the report, released on Wednesday, sets out what is needed to limit warming. That entails cutting global greenhouse gas emissions by 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, all compared with 2025 levels. This implies average annual reduction rates of 5.7% for 2025-2035, higher than the pathways laid out by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change in its last major scientific report, which required annual reduction rates of about 5%, UNEP said. Paris Agreement committee names three countries snubbing it over NDCs The more ambitious emissions reductions – which countries are still far off achieving – would put the world on the lowest-possible overshoot pathway, giving a 50% chance of limiting peak warming to 1.7–1.8C around mid-century before bringing global temperatures back to 1.5C or below by 2100, the report said. Reaching this scenario will also require carbon removal from the atmosphere, it added. UNEP noted that if countries fully implement their current national climate plans (NDCs), they would only reduce emissions by 5-8% by 2030 and 11-15% by 2035, relative to 2025 levels. UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen said the world must not give up on the Paris Agreement’s most ambitious warming limit, adding that every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of heating above 1.5C increases climate change impacts and risks, such as the deadly floods, heatwaves and wildfires that have plagued many nations this year. “We must pull out all the stops to minimise peak warming and return to 1.5C by the end of the century. This is possible,” she said, adding that governments must urgently implement policies that deliver rapid and sustained emissions reductions. Climate pledges fall short New climate pledges since last year’s report have made a negligible difference to projected emissions and warming, UNEP said. Under current policies, the world is on course for 2.8C of warming this century, while full implementation of national climate pledges and continued similar efforts would limit warming to 2.6C, the report found. UNEP said its projections had deteriorated, attributing this to the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement under President Donald Trump and revised estimates of historical emissions. Even with the most optimistic pledge-based scenario – which assumes countries deliver both their current national climate commitments and additional net-zero targets – warming would now only be limited to 2.1C this century, the report found. IPCC scientists vow to press on with climate reports despite political deadlock Speaking to journalists ahead of the report’s launch, co-author Anne Ohlhoff said the US exit from the Paris accord meant that its previous national climate target was no longer included in UNEP’s global projections. The country has also dropped its net-zero emissions goal, she said, affecting the outlook because the US is the world’s second-largest emitter. She warned that there is still a large gap between countries’ emissions commitments for 2035 and the reductions needed under the report’s lowest-possible 1.5C overshoot scenario. Every five years of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions at current levels pushes peak warming up by around 0.1C, she said, adding that without urgent action, it could quickly become impossible to keep peak warming below 1.7–1.8C. Describing the emissions gap as a “leadership gap”, UN chief Guterres warned that current national climate plans and policies “fall dangerously short” of what is needed to limit warming. He urged countries to adopt credible roadmaps for transitioning away from fossil fuels, accelerate clean energy deployment and electrification, invest in electricity grids and storage, cut methane emissions and halt deforestation. Carbon removal needed, but risky Alongside deep emissions cuts, removal of CO₂ from the atmosphere needs to be accelerated throughout the century, the report found. The world will need to remove and permanently store about 320 billion tonnes of CO₂ from the atmosphere to return global temperatures to around 1.5C by 2100. The estimated carbon removal is equivalent to around eight years of global CO₂ emissions at 2024 levels. However, UNEP cautions that removing carbon at this scale remains uncertain because of technological and socio-economic challenges. Keywan Riahi, a contributor to the report, said carbon could be removed through nature-based approaches, such as planting forests and improving wetland management, which help ecosystems absorb carbon emissions, as well as engineering solutions that capture emissions from energy production or remove carbon directly from the air. A view of Brazil’s Pantanal wetland (Photo: Silas Ismael/Wetlands International Brazil office) A view of Brazil’s Pantanal wetland (Photo: Silas Ismael/Wetlands International Brazil office) However, he warned that both nature-based and technological approaches face risks and might not deliver carbon removal at the scale needed. This is because nature solutions such as planetary sinks are weakening because of climate change while techno-fixes remain uncertain, he added. “All of those technologies come with risks,” Riahi told reporters, adding that what the world needs is to try “to keep the overshoot as low as possible, so that we do not need to rely on these technologies to take CO₂ out of the atmosphere later on”. Renewable energy supports emissions cuts Despite the expected overshoot of the 1.5C warming limit, the UNEP Emissions Gap Report underscored that the rapid growth of renewable energy and the impact of climate policies so far show that deeper emissions cuts remain possible. It stated that since the adoption of the Paris Agreement in 2015, global renewable electricity capacity has grown three times faster than anticipated, while solar photovoltaic (PV) deployment has increased sevenfold compared with projections made a decade ago. Maintaining the recent pace of renewable energy expansion, alongside stronger policies, could put the world on track to meet the global goal of tripling renewable energy capacity by 2030, the report said. It could also increase the share of wind and solar in electricity generation to levels consistent with the pathway that limits the overshoot of 1.5C to the lowest possible level, it added. SE Asia speeds up plan for connected clean power grid after oil shock Andersen said the explosion of renewable energy and slower-than-projected growth in coal energy supply showed that accelerating climate action is possible. However, she warned that progress remains insufficient, particularly in phasing down fossil fuels and halting forest loss. “Nations must understand that the point of return begins now, not later,” she said, calling for “fast, deep and sustained emissions reductions”. She urged governments to strengthen their climate action at upcoming UN climate talks and accelerate efforts to keep the 1.5C pathway within reach. Bill Hare, chief executive of Climate Analytics, said major fossil fuel-producing countries need to take greater responsibility for reducing their emissions, saying that big polluters such as the US and Saudi Arabia need “to stop playing politics and face the scientific reality”. “Right now they are looking at the fire, denying it exists and pouring more petrol on it, while their own citizens increasingly face searing heat, wildfires and other impacts,” he said. “Governments [need] to get on with enacting policies that cut fossil fuel use as soon as possible.” The post UN sets steep emission cuts to reverse 1.5C overshoot by end of century appeared first on Climate Home News.
summary: UN urges 6% annual cuts to reverse 1.5°C overshoot by 2100.
author: Climate Home News

title: Longyearbyen Faces Climate Crisis: Toxic Tap Water, Landslides, and Melting Glaciers
content:
Longyearbyen, a Norwegian village on the remote Arctic islands of Svalbard, is experiencing rapid warming. As glaciers melt and permafrost thaws, residents face climate‑induced problems from tap water to housebuilding to landslides. Heavy metals have made the village’s tap water toxic, according to recent reports.

Nearby, the Foxfonna glacier sits on a mountain 8 miles (15 km) from Longyearbyen. Glaciologist Andy Hodson points out the glacier’s distinctive “ears” of ice, which gave the glacier its name after the Arctic fox. The small glacier is a popular summer hike for tourists seeking an Arctic experience.
summary: Longyearbyen, a Norwegian village on the remote Arctic islands of Svalbard, is experiencing climate‑induced problems including toxic tap water, housebuilding challenges, and landslides. The village is near the Foxfonna glacier, which melts and is a popular summer hike for tourists, and a glaciologist named Andy Hodson has noted the glacier’s distinctive “ears” of ice.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Firefighters warn drought hampers water supply for UK wildfires after Stourbridge blaze
content: Firefighters in Stourbridge reported that a summer blaze destroyed homes and that low water pressure forced them to wait 40 minutes to fill a water carrier. The incident highlighted broader concerns about the UK’s capacity to manage wildfires amid drought conditions. After MPs were briefed on the difficulties firefighters faced during this year’s record summer, they urged the government to clarify water companies’ statutory responsibilities during major fire incidents. The aim is to strengthen the country’s preparedness for future wildfire threats.
summary: Low pressure during a summer fire that destroyed homes in Stourbridge meant filling a water carrier took 40 minutes. Firefighters said drought is straining water supplies and urged the government to set out water companies' statutory responsibilities for major fire incidents.
author: Guardian Environment

title: UN says world must cut emissions 18% in four years to stay within climate targets
content: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) has warned that the world must cut carbon emissions by nearly a fifth—about 18%—in the next four years to avoid a disastrous overshoot of climate targets. UNEP also says emissions need to be reduced by close to half within a decade. The agency notes that while the “window has closed” on keeping temperature rises to 1.5 °C, limiting the overshoot of that target remains possible.
summary: The UN Environment Programme says the world must cut carbon emissions by nearly a fifth in the next four years. It adds that emissions must be cut by close to half within a decade to avoid a disastrous overshoot of climate targets, even though the 1.5°C window has closed.
author: Guardian Environment

title: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
content:
The UK government has approved the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, a decision that was widely anticipated following lobbying by Shell. This move is expected to disappoint environmental campaigners and several Labour MPs, despite the party’s 2024 election manifesto commitment to ban new drilling licences in the region.

The companies behind Jackdaw and the separately decided Rosebank oilfield project have pursued environmental approval under existing licences. This approach allows them to proceed with operations despite the stated policy shift against new drilling permissions.
summary: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Five At-Home Strength Moves Can Make Everyday Tasks Easier
content:
Functional strength training can help make everyday tasks easier. The Cleveland Clinic notes that when you need two trips to bring groceries in or feel winded after climbing stairs, it highlights the importance of everyday strength.

Unlike isolated exercises such as a biceps curl, functional moves engage several joints and muscle groups simultaneously. This approach mirrors the way the body moves in daily life, improving overall functional capacity.
summary: The Cleveland Clinic explains that functional strength training uses moves that work several joints and muscle groups together, mimicking daily body movements. These at-home strength moves can reduce the effort needed for tasks like carrying groceries or climbing stairs.
author: Medical Xpress

title: FDA approves Jemperli immunotherapy for untreated rectal cancer patients
content: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the immunotherapy Jemperli (dostarlimab‑gxly) on Monday for certain adults with untreated rectal cancer. The approval could allow some patients to avoid chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery.
summary: Some people with rectal cancer may now be able to skip chemotherapy, radiation and surgery. The U.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Patients with Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases Face Higher Long COVID Risk
content: A recent study published online on Oct. 14 in Arthritis & Rheumatology reports that patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases (AIRD) face an increased risk of developing long COVID. The research highlights a higher likelihood of prolonged post‑viral symptoms in this patient population.
summary: A study published online Oct. 14 in Arthritis & Rheumatology found that patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases (AIRD) have an increased risk for long COVID. The study identifies a higher susceptibility to long COVID among AIRD patients.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Rethinking Parkinson's gait rehabilitation through wearable sensing and virtual reality
content: Researchers are exploring Parkinson’s gait rehabilitation by combining wearable sensors with virtual reality. Sensors embedded in wearable technology record a person’s real‑world movements while they step into a virtual environment. This approach provides a detailed view of how Parkinson’s disease affects movement and offers insights that could lead to more effective treatments.
summary: Researchers use wearable sensors to track Parkinson's disease patients' movement outside a virtual world. The data provides a detailed view of how the disease affects gait and offers insight into more effective treatment.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Early RA treat-to-target strategy linked to better 10‑year outcomes
content: A study published online Oct. 15 in Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases found that early rheumatoid arthritis patients managed with a treat‑to‑target strategy who achieved sustained remission at two years experienced higher remission rates and better physical function at ten years.
summary: A study published online Oct. 15 in Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases found that patients with early rheumatoid arthritis who achieved sustained remission at two years had higher remission rates at ten years. The study also reported better physical function at ten years for those patients.
author: Medical Xpress

title: An extra serving of fruit linked to lower risk of depression and anxiety in teenagers
content: New research from the University of Sydney shows that teenagers’ food choices, including sugar consumption, are linked to the later emergence of depression and anxiety symptoms. An additional serving of fruit, in particular, is associated with a lower risk of developing these mental health conditions.
summary: The food choices teenagers make could have implications beyond their physical health, with new research from the University of Sydney linking food choices and sugar consumption to the later emergence of depression and anxiety symptoms.
author: Medical Xpress

title: First-in-human study of dual-imaging catheter to assess heart attack risk, guide treatment
content:
Researchers at the UC Davis National Center for Interventional Biophotonic Technologies (NCIBT) have concluded the first‑in‑human test of a new device that could help doctors better detect and treat atherosclerosis, the narrowing of blood vessels due to plaque buildup.  

The flexible catheter‑based device, developed at NCIBT labs, is designed to navigate the interior walls of arteries and capture detailed information about plaque buildup in real time.
summary: Researchers at the UC Davis National Center for Interventional Biophotonic Technologies concluded the first-in-human test of a flexible catheter‑based device. The device navigates artery walls and captures real‑time detailed plaque information to help detect and treat atherosclerosis.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Rare solar radiation storm provides clearest picture of flight risks
content: A rare solar radiation storm produced the most comprehensive data set ever gathered from Earth's atmosphere, according to new research led by the University of Surrey. The study shows that coordinated radiation monitoring is essential for aviation safety, providing the clearest picture yet of flight risks posed by such solar events.
summary: The study collected the most comprehensive data set ever from Earth's atmosphere during a solar radiation event. It highlights the need for better-coordinated radiation monitoring to improve aviation safety, according to research led by the University of Surrey.
author: Phys.org

title: Major repairs needed to save Horseshoe Bay Lagoon
content:
A study by volunteer researcher Chris Hopper, JCU adjunct professor Eric Wolanski, and independent researcher Natalie K. Dowling examined the impact of saltwater and erosion on Horseshoe Bay Lagoon, a freshwater lagoon on the island. The research was published in the journal Applied Sciences.

The authors noted that Horseshoe Bay Lagoon is one of the few swamps on the island that contains bulkuru sedge, also known as water chestnut.
summary: Volunteer researcher Chris Hopper, JCU's adjunct professor Eric Wolanski and independent researcher Natalie K. Dowling examined the impact of saltwater and erosion on Horseshoe Bay Lagoon, a freshwater lagoon and one of the few swamps with bulkuru sedge—also known as water chestnut—on the island.
author: Phys.org

title: Controlled vapor treatment yields highly oriented soft quasicrystals
content: A controlled vapor treatment has been shown to direct molecules to form highly oriented soft quasicrystals. While molecules can spontaneously self‑assemble into complex ordered structures, soft quasicrystals exhibit non‑repeating patterns, and achieving uniform orientation across large areas has been a major challenge. The vapor‑based approach addresses this difficulty.
summary: Controlled vapor treatment was used to guide molecules to self‑assemble into highly oriented soft quasicrystals. Achieving uniform orientation of these structures over large areas has been a major challenge.
author: Phys.org

title: Women farmers need better financing to access AI technologies
content: Women farmers require improved financing to fully leverage digital technologies and artificial intelligence. The source calls for public and private investments to remove financial barriers that limit women’s access to these tools, noting that multiple global crises and reductions in aid are intensifying the challenge.
summary: Public and private investments must address financial barriers that stop women from fully benefiting from digital technologies and artificial intelligence. These barriers are heightened by multiple global crises and aid cuts.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds magnetar can be born when two neutron stars touch
content:
A new study posted on the arXiv preprint server proposes that a magnetar can be born when two neutron stars touch. The paper examines how the extreme magnetic fields of neutron stars might be amplified in such a contact event, offering a possible formation pathway for magnetars.

Neutron stars typically possess magnetic fields about 100,000 times stronger than the strongest fields created on Earth, and roughly 1 % of them have fields 1,000 times stronger, classifying them as magnetars. Magnetars are considered likely sources of powerful transient phenomena such as soft gamma‑ray repeaters and fast radio bursts.
summary: Magnetars are a rare type of neutron star, making up about 1% of neutron stars and possessing magnetic fields roughly 1,000 times stronger than typical neutron stars. A new study posted on the arXiv preprint server suggests that a magnetar can be born when two neutron stars touch.
author: Phys.org

title: Guatemala adds first endemic bird in AOS 67th supplement
content: The American Ornithological Society’s 67th Supplement to its Check‑list of North American Birds was released today in the journal Ornithology. The supplement provides several significant classification updates for birds of North America, Central America and the Caribbean, and marks the first time Guatemala is recorded as having an endemic bird species.
summary: The American Ornithological Society's 67th Supplement to its Check‑list of North American Birds was published today in Ornithology. The supplement records Guatemala's first endemic bird among several classification updates for species in North America, Central America and the Caribbean.
author: Phys.org

title: UN says 1.5°C target exceeded, world on track for 2.8°C warming
content: The United Nations has stated that the planet has already surpassed the 1.5 °C warming threshold and is now on a trajectory toward 2.8 °C of global temperature rise. It notes that the best‑case scenario would only allow a temporary breach of 1.5 °C, but current climate pledges are insufficient to keep warming within that limit.
summary: The UN reports that the planet will only temporarily breach 1.5°C of warming. Current climate pledges fall way short of that hope.
author: New Scientist

title: Bad apple effect: study shows how people are influenced by rule-breaking of others
content: Research shows how seeing bigger violations by others can lead people to increase their own rule-breaking From politicians taking bribes to bullying and harassment in City firms, leaders have been quick to label those who break the rules as the odd “bad apple”. But new research backs up the idiom that one bad apple can spoil the barrel. Researchers have found that when people go beyond the rule-breaking they see in others, general compliance can swiftly turn into widespread rule-breaking.
summary: Research shows that seeing larger violations by others can lead people to increase their own rule-breaking. The study finds that when people go beyond the rule-breaking they see in others, general compliance can swiftly turn into widespread rule-breaking.
author: Guardian Science

title: Extratropical Cyclone Whips Past Iceland
content:
An extratropical cyclone moved across the North Atlantic and brushed past Iceland on the afternoon of October 14, 2026. The storm was captured by the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on the NOAA‑21 satellite, and the resulting image was published by NASA’s Earth Observatory. The system originated from the remnants of Hurricane Isaias, which had made landfall in Florida as a Category 2 hurricane on October 9, 2026, before tracking eastward along the jet stream.

During its passage near Iceland, the cyclone’s central pressure fell by more than 50 hectopascals in a 24‑hour period, a rate that exceeds the threshold for explosive cyclogenesis, also known as bombogenesis. Some meteorologists noted that, after correcting for altitude, the pressure may have set a new October low for Iceland, potentially breaking a record that had stood since 1963.

The storm produced extreme wind conditions across the island. A gust of 205 kilometers per hour (128 mph) was recorded near the Eyjafjallajökull volcano in southern Iceland, while a nearby offshore island experienced sustained winds of 150 kilometers per hour (93 mph). High winds also affected northern parts of the country, where residents faced sleet and snow as the cyclone passed.

Further east, northwestern Scotland recorded gusts up to 90 kilometers per hour (55 mph) on the same day, prompting cancellations on several ferry routes, according to news reports. The event was documented in a NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using VIIRS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE, GIBS/Worldview, and the Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS). The accompanying story was written by Lindsey Doermann.
summary: Extratropical Cyclone Whips Past Iceland.
author: NASA News

title: New ghost-like nebulas discovered in Cassiopeia constellation
content:
A new Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) dated October 21, 2026, features an image of the Cassiopeia constellation that reveals three faint nebulas. The image was captured by Louis Leroux-Géré, Thibault Rouillée, Vincent Martin, and Cédric de Decker of Starfront Observatories after 100 hours of observation using a special oxygen filter. The accompanying explanation, written by Keighley Rockcliffe, Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, and Cecilia Chirenti, highlights these newly discovered objects alongside the well-known IC 59 and IC 63, known as the original Ghosts of Cassiopeia.

The original ghosts are located near the multi-star system γ Cassiopeia. Energetic light from this system causes hydrogen gas in IC 59 and 63 to glow red, while dust in the region reflects and scatters blue-ish white starlight. In contrast, the newly identified Objects 1, 2, and 3 appear as blue phantoms, indicating the presence of ionized oxygen. The source notes that the specific agent ionizing this oxygen remains a question for astronomers.

The explanation proposes that γ Cassiopeia may be piling up material as it moves through interstellar gas and dust, similar to the bow of a speeding boat. It suggests that Object 3 could be the compressed and heated oxygen resulting from this bow shock. Additionally, Object 1 might be a planetary nebula if a central white dwarf is identified. The text concludes that the origins of these astronomical apparitions remain a mystery to be solved. The image is a service of ASD at NASA / GSFC, NASA Science Activation, and Michigan Tech. U.
summary: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 21 – New… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.
author: NASA News

title: Tomás Villalón Jr. co‑founds Phoenix Tailings to extract rare earths from waste
content:
Tomás Villalón Jr. ’14, a native of San Antonio, Texas, grew up in Monterrey, Mexico, a city known for steel manufacturing. He recalls the smog that once hung over the city and says that experience motivated him to pursue sustainable metallurgy. Villalón earned a degree in materials science and engineering and, during his senior year, began thinking about decarbonizing steelmaking while working at Boston Metal, an MIT spinoff.

In 2019, Villalón co‑founded Phoenix Tailings. The company has developed an efficient process for extracting rare earth metals from mining waste. Villalón serves as chief technology officer, and the founding team also includes Michelle Chao ’17, Nick Myers, and Anthony Balladon. Phoenix Tailings claims its proprietary electrochemical technique produces no toxins and is carbon‑free when powered by renewable energy.

For more information, visit www.technologyreview.com/alumni-profiles.
summary: Tomás Villalón Jr., a materials science and engineering graduate, co‑founded Phoenix Tailings in 2019 to develop an efficient, carbon‑free electrochemical process for extracting rare earth metals from mining waste. He serves as chief technology officer, and the company says its technique generates no toxins when powered by renewables.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Alissa Totman leads brain injury nonprofit Synapse and practices at UPMC
content: Alissa Totman ’13 was a sophomore when she joined MIT BrainTrust, a student-run organization that connects Institute undergraduates and people with brain injuries for support and socializing. “That group was a great way to learn about the human experience of what people go through when they experience a brain injury,” she says. And it laid the foundation for her life’s work. Today, Totman is a physician specializing in brain injury medicine at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, where she treats adults with head trauma, stroke, brain tumors, and more. She is also the founder of Synapse, a nonprofit focused on providing support for such individuals. The organization grew out of a group she started with Jaclyn Konopka ’14 during medical school at Stanford, and Totman launched it as a national service organization in 2016, while pursuing her master’s degree in public health at Harvard. There are now chapters at 28 universities across the country—and Totman still runs the organization. “There’s a big need for more resources like this,” she says. Read more at www. Technologyreview. Com/alumni-profiles.
summary: Alissa Totman ’13, who joined MIT BrainTrust as a sophomore, is now a physician specializing in brain injury medicine at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. She founded the nonprofit Synapse, which launched nationally in 2016 while she was earning a master’s in public health at Harvard and now has chapters at 28 universities.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: YouTube testing hiding dislike button by moving it to three‑dot menu
content:
YouTube appears to be testing a change that would hide the dislike button on videos, according to a report by 9to5Google. Several users on X have posted screenshots showing the dislike button moved into the three‑dots submenu, and a Reddit user shared an image where the button is missing entirely.  

In the current interface the dislike button sits directly next to the like button beneath a video. By relocating it to a submenu, YouTube would make it more difficult to access, potentially reducing its use. The writer notes that this move follows earlier changes: the dislike counter was removed, the button was removed from YouTube Shorts, and now the dislike button is being hidden.
summary: YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, with screenshots posted by users on X showing it placed in the three‑dot submenu. A Reddit user also shared an image where the dislike button is absent, while it currently sits next to the like button under videos.
author: The Verge

title: Meta ordered to disclose executives who approved torrent downloads for AI training
content: In copyright lawsuits over AI training, Meta has spent weeks blaming staff for downloading torrents. The company has now been ordered to name executives who authorized decisions to pirate books from shadow libraries like Anna’s Archive and LibGen, TorrentFreak reported. In a discovery order impacting a class action raised by book authors—including Richard Kadrey and Sarah Silverman—as well as a lawsuit from publisher Entrepreneur Media, Magistrate Judge Thomas Hixon largely agreed that Meta must clearly identify key decision-makers. Following testimony from Meta staff who downloaded torrents, the order could expose a wider range of supervisors, managers, and executives whom staffers said greenlit the piracy. Meta had been hoping to avoid detailing the chain of command, particularly for leadership involved in early AI training. According to a Meta court filing, its initial efforts to compile massive AI datasets were managed through an “informal approach" where supposedly nobody with authority made any decisions. Instead, Meta insisted that a “decision” was “made only in the sense” that some staffers “technically” downloaded torrents. Read full article Comments
summary: In copyright lawsuits over AI training, Meta has spent weeks blaming staff for downloading torrents. The company has now been ordered to name executives who authorized decisions to pirate books from shadow libraries like Anna’s Archive and LibGen, TorrentFreak reported.
author: Ars Technica

title: Quantinuum says its hardware scales beyond breakeven, performance improves >10×
content:
Quantinuum announced on Monday that its current generation of quantum‑computing hardware can scale logical qubits well beyond the breakeven point. The company said that each increase in the size of a logical qubit improves certain performance metrics by a factor of more than ten.

The announcement comes amid broader discussion of quantum error correction, where collections of hardware qubits are linked to detect and correct errors. While adding more hardware qubits to a logical qubit can improve error detection, it also raises the chance of new errors if the underlying hardware error rate is too high. Several firms have shown logical qubits that surpass the breakeven threshold, though the gains have generally been modest. Quantinuum’s claim of a ten‑fold improvement per scaling step suggests a more pronounced performance boost than previously reported.
summary: On Monday Quantinuum announced its current generation of quantum hardware can scale well beyond the breakeven point for logical qubits. Each increase in logical‑qubit size improved certain performance measures by a factor of more than ten.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ukraine uses hexacopter drone to evacuate wounded soldier from frontline
content:
Ukraine’s army released video footage of an unprecedented drone rescue that lifted a wounded soldier from the frontline and flew him to safety. The operation, shown in a clip posted on October 19, depicts the soldier fastening a harness beneath a heavy hexacopter drone with six rotors before being lifted away. Ukrainian sources said the mission occurred at an undisclosed time and location where Russian drones and landmines made the use of a wheeled ground robot impractical, according to The Kyiv Independent.

The rescue follows recent deployment of Ukrainian drones designed for casualty evacuation, marking a step beyond the United States military’s decades of experimentation with similar concepts. “This is a historic event, the next stage of evacuating the wounded, which we will all come to,” said Napalm, a programmer with the 92nd separate assault brigade’s unmanned ground systems company, adding that systematic work will now aim to make such missions routine.
summary: Ukraine’s unprecedented drone rescue of a wounded soldier from the battlefield has shown once again how battlefield necessity can spur innovation. The operation was revealed just days after separate Ukrainian drones designed for casualty evacuation were deployed for frontline testing—taking a step beyond the US military’s decades of experimentation with similar concepts.
author: Ars Technica

title: Antares remains last US medium‑lift rocket as new generation arrives
content:
The Antares medium‑lift rocket, developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation, made its United States debut 13 years ago. Its first 100‑series version relied on refurbished Soviet‑era engines originally built during the Apollo Moon‑landing period; Aerojet acquired and updated those engines in the 1990s for use on Antares. After four successful flights, the vehicle suffered an explosion on its fifth launch in 2014.

Antares is described as the last example of a declining class of U.S. medium‑lift launchers, defined as rockets capable of delivering 2 to 20 metric tons to orbit. The vehicle’s design also incorporated a core stage manufactured in Ukraine. A new generation of medium‑lift rockets is now emerging, differing markedly from Antares in both propulsion and manufacturing origins.
summary: It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation. The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess.
author: Ars Technica

title: TP-Link pledges to assemble Wi‑Fi routers in US to win Trump administration approval
content: TP-Link yesterday announced plans to assemble Wi-Fi routers in the US, as the company attempts to get the Trump administration's approval to sell its newest routers to American consumers. The timing is uncertain, as TP-Link's press release said it expects US-based assembly to begin "as early as" 2027. TP-Link's application to sell new routers in the US could be rejected by the Trump administration or remain pending long enough to push the US-based assembly to 2028. "Pending US regulatory approval, TP-Link expects domestic assembly of its groundbreaking Wi-Fi 8 home networking product line to begin as early as next year," the company said. TP-Link said it signed a Letter of Intent with US company Keytronic, which agreed "to become a primary domestic manufacturing partner for TP-Link, supporting assembly of the company’s advanced networking portfolio in Corinth, Mississippi." Read full article Comments
summary: TP-Link yesterday announced plans to assemble Wi-Fi routers in the US, as the company attempts to get the Trump administration's approval to sell its newest routers to American consumers. The timing is uncertain, as TP-Link's press release said it expects US-based assembly to begin "as early as" 2027.
author: Ars Technica

title: PHP to release two emergency patches for critical 9.2‑severity bugs within 12 hours
content:
PHP maintainers announced on Monday that they intend to issue emergency patches for two vulnerabilities, each rated 9.2 out of 10 in severity, in a little more than 12 hours. The advisory urges all PHP users to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the releases become available.

The maintainers added that they may release the patches earlier if details of either vulnerability become public or if evidence of active exploitation emerges in the wild.
summary: Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
author: Ars Technica

title: London wikithon brings volunteers together to edit Wikipedia arms‑trade pages
content:
A recent “wikithon” in a central London classroom brought together roughly two dozen volunteers for a day of collective Wikipedia editing. Participants, ranging from veteran editors in their 70s to students who had never registered an account, worked at laptops while enjoying free vegan Ethiopian food.

The event highlights the fact that only a relatively small number of people actually edit Wikipedia, despite the site’s 270,000 active volunteers who contribute content on topics from 19th‑century medicine to TikTok trends. Many subjects—particularly those related to the global south and notable women—remain underrepresented.

This group of new recruits is focusing on the arms industry, a topic that has been largely neglected. Their editing targets include companies and projects such as Palantir, Project Maven, and Nitro‑Chem.
summary: Volunteers and new recruits gathered for a “wikithon” in a central London classroom to edit Wikipedia pages on the arms industry. Participants, ranging from veteran editors in their 70s to students new to Wikipedia, worked on topics such as Palantir, Project Maven and Nitro‑Chem while receiving free vegan Ethiopian food.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Morning news bulletin October 21, 2026 covers Europe and global stories
content: The October 21, 2026 morning bulletin highlights the most important stories from across Europe and beyond. It covers breaking news in the world, business, entertainment, politics, culture, and travel, offering a concise overview of the day’s key events.
summary: Morning news bulletin October 21, 2026 covers Europe and global stories.
author: Euronews

title: French PM Sebastien Lecornu pledges massive police presence for weekend protests
content:
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu announced on Tuesday that a “massive” police presence would be deployed for fresh protests scheduled for the coming weekend. The announcement came amid criticism of his government’s handling of recent street violence.

The country’s second‑largest eurozone economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before voters head to the polls to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron. The report was provided by FRANCE 24’s Ellen Gainsford.
summary: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Tuesday he will ensure a massive police presence at the protests scheduled for the coming weekend. The protests follow Saturday's severe rioting, one of the worst in recent years, occurring six months before the presidential election.
author: France 24

title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case
content: Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case, occurring amid an outbreak that started in the Democratic Republic of Congo in mid‑May. The confirmation was announced during the evening programme.
summary: In tonight's programme, Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case in the midst of an outbreak that began in DRC Congo in mid-May. Also, a former top South African police officer facing sexual grooming and rape charges is denied bail.
author: France 24

title: Bipartisan voter pushback targets data centers ahead of US midterms
content:
Two weeks before the U.S. midterm elections, voters and lawmakers are voicing bipartisan concerns about data centers that consume large amounts of water and power. The pushback highlights worries that these facilities drain local resources and impact communities.

Just two years earlier, ChatGPT was a new technology and many voters admired AI with awe. In swing districts, the primary issue remains economic, with inflation and the “price of eggs” cited as the most pressing concerns. Voter anxiety now also includes broader worries about global stability.

Looking ahead to 2026, bots and large language models are expected to write academic papers and produce campaign advertisements. Calls for regulation are rising, even as tech billionaires resist. Recent stock‑market volatility has prompted questions about whether the rapid expansion of AI and data‑center infrastructure may be reaching limits.
summary: Two weeks before the midterm elections, voters from both parties are opposing data centers that consume local water and power. The backlash coincides with growing use of bots and large language models to write papers and campaign ads, prompting calls for regulation despite resistance from tech billionaires.
author: France 24

title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case as outbreak spreads in Africa
content: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in Africa's latest outbreak, while Kenya reported its ninth infection, heightening concerns about further spread across the continent. Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya warned of an “extremely serious threat” and urged the international community to send funding, medical supplies, and health workers.
summary: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case as outbreak spreads in Africa.
author: France 24

title: Italy to deploy 500 soldiers after Milan riots injure 100 police
content:
Italy announced tougher security measures after weekend riots in Milan that left over 100 police officers injured and shops looted.  

The government will deploy 500 additional soldiers, impose harsher penalties for violent protesters, and hold parents financially responsible for damage caused by minors.
summary: Italy announced tougher security measures on Tuesday after weekend riots in Milan left more than 100 police officers injured and shops looted. The government will deploy 500 additional soldiers, impose harsher penalties for violent protesters and hold parents financially responsible for damage caused by minors.
author: France 24

title: French PM Sébastien Lecornu to meet unions on protest security ahead of new protests
content: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is set to meet trade‑union organisations on Wednesday to discuss security measures for protests and the response to high‑school students who sparked the now‑nationwide demonstrations. The talks follow the introduction of curfews in French cities aimed at halting further weekend violence and looting.
summary: After imposing curfews in cities across France to curb weekend violence and looting, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is set to meet trade union organisations on Wednesday. The meeting will focus on protest security and the response to the high‑school students who sparked the nationwide protests.
author: France 24

title: US envoy Steve Witkoff to meet Putin in Saint Petersburg after talks with Zelensky
content: U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff is scheduled to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday, following discussions with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo. According to Axios, Witkoff will deliver an updated peace proposal aimed at ending the war in Ukraine.
summary: US special envoy Steve Witkoff will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday after speaking with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo. Axios reported that Witkoff will present Putin with an updated peace proposal to end the war in Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: EU unveils Arctic plan, cites drone, GPS and cable threats, eyes Russia, US competition
content: The European Union has presented a new set of Arctic priorities, positioning itself alongside Russia, China and the United States in a competition for influence in the region. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas warned that drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage are undermining Arctic security.
summary: The EU unveiled its Arctic priorities as it competes with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage threaten Arctic security.
author: DW World

title: Fifth foreign firm pulls out of controversial Israeli East Jerusalem cable car plan
content:
A fifth foreign company has withdrawn from a plan to construct a 1.4‑kilometre cable car linking West Jerusalem with East Jerusalem. Rights groups contend that the route, which would terminate at a compound operated by the far‑right settler organization Elad, could lead to the seizure of land and property belonging to dozens of Palestinian families and alter the cultural landscape of the area.

Local authorities say the project will continue despite the withdrawal. After a four‑year pause, the Jerusalem Development Authority announced in late September—just weeks before Israel’s 27 October elections—that it intended to award the contract without a public tender to ROPES, a cable‑car engineering consultancy based in South Tyrol, Italy. The authority maintains that the scheme remains on schedule.
summary: Fifth foreign firm pulls out of controversial Israeli East Jerusalem cable car plan.
author: Guardian World

title: Iranian ferry captain steers half‑full vessel through war‑torn Strait of Hormuz
content:
Despite ongoing US‑Israeli airstrikes and Tehran’s attacks on shipping, the Strait of Hormuz continues to serve as a vital lifeline for residents and workers in the region, according to the report.  

Captain Farouq steered a ferry departing the terminal at Bandar Abbas, noting the terminal’s lights receding as the vessel left. The ferry, operating at roughly half capacity with about 100 passengers, proceeded into the darkness of the strait while its navigation radar emitted periodic beeps and displayed green and pink lights. The captain then pulled the vessel into deeper waters.
summary: US‑Israeli airstrikes and Tehran’s attacks on shipping continue, yet the Strait of Hormuz still serves as a lifeline for people who live and work there. Capt Farouq guided a ferry from the Bandar Abbas terminal, carrying roughly 100 passengers at about half capacity, into the darkness of the strait’s deeper waters.
author: Guardian World

title: Serbian student movement Student List to field candidates in parliamentary vote
content:
A Serbian student movement called Student List has been holding continuous protests for two years, confronting the ruling party’s twelve‑year tenure. Volunteers from the group have been canvassing Belgrade’s Krnjača suburb, wearing “victory” lanyards, using a questionnaire and a mobile app to record household visits and gauge support.

This weekend, the movement will present its own candidates in the parliamentary elections, which the source describes as the most serious challenge Aleksandar Vučić has faced during his twelve years in power. The effort is framed as an unorthodox democratic experiment aimed at testing the ruling party’s dominance.
summary: Serbian student movement Student List to field candidates in parliamentary vote.
author: Guardian World

title: NextDC delays West Footscray datacentre expansion to 2027/28 after power pole protest
content:
Australia’s largest datacentre operator, NextDC, said its plan to double the size of the West Footscray (M3) datacentre in Melbourne’s west has been delayed. The company told the Australian Stock Exchange that community objections to 22‑metre‑high power poles have halted Jemena’s upgrade of the poles, which are required to supply the additional electricity for the expansion. As a result, the project is now expected to be completed in the 2027/2028 financial year.

The construction pause triggered a sharp fall in NextDC’s share price following the announcement. The delay is linked directly to the stalled power‑pole upgrade and the associated community protest.
summary: NextDC told the Australian Stock Exchange that the expansion of its M3 datacentre in west Melbourne has been delayed. The delay, caused by a pause in Jemena’s upgrade of 22‑metre power poles after community protest, pushes the project to the 2027/2028 financial year.
author: Guardian World

title: No bail set for Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of febrile political climate
content: AFP commissioner says MPs are generally concerned about growing volume of abuse and intimidation Follow our live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The head of the Australian federal police has condemned a “febrile” political environment that has seen one person charged every week over the alleged threatening of MPs, as Victoria announces new steps to protect politicians. But the AFP and Victoria police insist they had no intelligence to suggest 43-year-old Brendan Nugent would go on to allegedly drive a Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP Helen Haines in a targeted attack.
summary: No bail set for Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of febrile political climate.
author: Guardian World

title: AFP warns Australia of AI‑driven surge in youth crime and rapid radicalisation
content:
Australia is confronting a “tsunami” of youth crime, according to a parliamentary inquiry that highlighted the role of artificial intelligence in speeding up radicalisation. The inquiry noted that children as young as 12 have been among dozens of young people targeted by federal police operations since 2020.

During the hearing, Australian federal police acting deputy commissioner Sandra Booth explained that the traditional radicalisation process, which previously took years or months, can now occur within days due to AI‑driven influences.
summary: Children as young as 12 have been among dozens targeted in federal police operations since 2020, according to a parliamentary inquiry. AFP acting deputy commissioner Sandra Booth told the inquiry that AI can now accelerate radicalisation from years or months to within days.
author: Guardian World

title: Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly played Taylor Swift’s No Body, No Crime during body disposal, court told
content: Beau Lamarre‑Condon is alleged to have played Taylor Swift’s song “No Body, No Crime” while attempting to dispose of two corpses, a NSW Supreme Court heard. A friend of the accused told the court that the van he was driving to Bungonia with a companion contained a lemony smell and a blue tarp in the back before stopping at a Bunnings store. The testimony linked the music and the described conditions to the alleged disposal attempt.
summary: Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly played Taylor Swift’s No Body, No Crime during body disposal, court told.
author: Guardian World

title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case in Abuja woman who arrived from Uganda
content:
Nigeria’s health ministry confirmed an Ebola case in the capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus. The confirmation comes as the outbreak spreads into western Africa.

The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October, was admitted to an Abuja hospital four days later and was subsequently diagnosed with Ebola. It remains unclear when she entered Nigeria, the continent’s most populous country.
summary: Nigeria's health ministry confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja after a woman who traveled from Uganda tested positive. The woman showed symptoms on 7 October, was admitted to an Abuja hospital four days later, and was later diagnosed with Ebola; her arrival date in Nigeria is unclear.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump aims to turn 106-year-old DC golf course into tournament venue, locals protest
content: Donald Trump announced plans to convert a 106‑year‑old public golf course in Washington, D.C., into a tournament‑capable venue for professional players. Local golfers, however, expressed displeasure with the proposal.
summary: Trump said he plans to convert a 106-year-old public golf course in Washington, DC into a tournament‑capable course for professional golfers. Local golfers have expressed unhappiness with the proposal.
author: BBC World

title: Haitian migrants changed this US town - Trump's deportation drive is reshaping it again
content: Springfield, Ohio, was thrust into national attention when the president promoted a false claim that pets were being eaten there. Years later, Haitian migrants have altered the community, and a renewed deportation effort by the president is again reshaping the town, which continues to sit at the center of the immigration debate.
summary: The president thrust Springfield, Ohio, into the spotlight with a false pet-eating claim - years later, it remains at the heart of the immigration debate.
author: BBC World

title: Elon Musk says Tesla‑SpaceX merger would bring many gains and be biggest ever
content: Elon Musk, the chief executive of both Tesla and SpaceX, says a merger of the two firms would yield “a lot to be gained” and would represent the biggest merger in history.
summary: Musk, who is CEO of both Tesla and SpaceX, says there is a lot to be gained from a merger of the two companies. He adds the proposed merger would be the biggest in history.
author: BBC World

title: Alberta vote to stay in Canada gives Mark Carney backing to confront Trump
content: Alberta held an overwhelming vote to remain in Canada. According to BBC’s Lyse Doucet, the result provides Mark Carney with political capital to focus on remaking the country’s economy and gives him backing to take on Trump.
summary: Alberta held an overwhelming vote to remain part of Canada. The result gives Mark Carney political capital to take on Trump and to focus on remaking the country's economy, writes BBC's Lyse Doucet.
author: BBC World

title: You Can See Everything buzz lifts Hulu's The Dropout viewership 186%
content:
The release of the documentary You Can See Everything has intensified public interest in the Theranos fraud saga. The film, described as record‑breaking, has drawn attention to the story of Elizabeth Holmes and the scandal that surrounded her former company.

According to Variety, viewership for Hulu’s 2022 series The Dropout, which stars Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, jumped 186 % in September versus the previous month. The surge followed the announcement on 6 September of the documentary’s first teaser.
summary: Interest in Elizabeth Holmes and the Theranos fraud scandal surged amid buzz for the record‑breaking documentary You Can See Everything. Viewership for Hulu’s 2022 series The Dropout, starring Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, rose 186% in September versus the prior month, according to Variety after the film’s first teaser was announced on 6 September.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Champions League roundup: McTominay double leads Napoli past Bodø/Glimt
content:
Scott McTominay scored his first two goals of the season to help Napoli defeat Bodø/Glimt 4-3, easing pressure on coach Massimiliano Allegri. The midfielder, who also hit a post, returned after missing a month following early September surgery to treat an irregular heartbeat. Matteo Politano opened the scoring in the first minute, but Bodø’s Jens Petter Hauge equalized. McTominay restored Napoli’s lead before halftime, only for Andreas Helmersen to level the score again for the Norwegian club.

In another match, ten-man Atlético Madrid secured a draw against Stuttgart.
summary: Champions League roundup: McTominay double leads Napoli past Bodø/Glimt.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
content:
Jonathan Wilson argues that Brighton should target a Champions League place, challenging the common perception that the club, along with Brentford and Bournemouth, is limited to upper mid-table finishes. Wilson notes that while these teams are often praised for making the most of limited resources, there is an underlying assumption that they lack higher aspirations.

The article highlights Diego Gómez’s recent goal in a "five-star demolition" as part of Brighton’s impressive run of results. Wilson suggests that the current season offers a unique opportunity for Brighton to break away from their established reputation. He points out that, aside from Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Specifically, Wilson mentions that Manchester City, despite starting the season with seven straight wins, may be removed from the top-five race due to potential penalties for breaching Premier League regulations. In this context, Wilson questions why one of these efficient smaller sides should not qualify for the Champions League.
summary: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lamine Yamal scores as Barcelona beat Real Betis in La Liga
content: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that, whatever that was, in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote.
summary: Lamine Yamal scored the opening goal in the ninth minute as La Liga leaders Barcelona defeated Real Betis. The 19-year-old was substituted in the 90th minute, receiving praise from coach Hansi Flick for his performance.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Foden Hat-Trick Powers Manchester City's Victory Over AEK Athens
content:
Phil Foden scored a hat-trick to lead Manchester City to a decisive victory over AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium. The win served as a response to manager Enzo Maresca’s call for the team to make its own noise amid recent distractions, helping the club regain momentum in the Champions League following a loss to Paris Saint-Germain. The match was played in front of an official attendance of 40,042, which was 20,000 fewer than the crowd that witnessed the previous weekend’s win over Ipswich.

Foden demonstrated his return to form by performing effectively on the right wing and as a central striker, proving the team’s depth with Erling Haaland watching from the bench. The opposition was outmatched by the Premier League side, which also saw goals from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. AEK Athens managed a consolation goal through Stavros Pilios, a result attributed in the report to the atmosphere created by their supporters rather than the visitors' overall performance.
summary: Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City defeated AEK Athens in a Champions League match. Erling Haaland watched from the bench while Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki also scored for the home side.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mac Allister double helps Liverpool beat Villarreal in Champions League
content: Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of a Champions League contest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum. Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third for Villarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez.
summary: Liverpool recovered from a two-goal deficit to defeat Villarreal, with Alexis Mac Allister scoring twice and Florian Wirtz adding his first goal of the season. The match featured a dramatic turnaround after Sergi Cardona's mistake and Ronald Araújo's equalizer, though Tani Oluwaseyi scored a late third goal for Villarreal.
author: Guardian Sport

title: PSG defeat Barcelona 4-2 in Champions League
content:
Paris Saint-Germain defeated Barcelona 4-2 in a Champions League match at the Parc des Princes. The article describes the encounter as a dazzling, open, and exhibition-style game between the French and Spanish champions. Although PSG was pegged back to a 2-2 draw midway through the second half, they ultimately secured the victory. The piece notes that for both teams, the primary stakes involved TV income and a semi-guaranteed place in the knockout stages, rather than high-risk competitive pressure.

The report highlights the attacking energy of PSG and the frailty of the Barcelona backline as the main takeaways from the match. It characterizes the atmosphere as one of fire, noise, and fury, suggesting that the scoreline was secondary to the quality of the football displayed. The article frames the event as a midweek A-game where the performance style mattered more than the final result.
summary: Paris Saint-Germain secured a 4-2 victory over Barcelona at the Parc des Princes after trailing 2-2 midway through the second half. The match highlighted the fragility of Barcelona's backline while showcasing PSG's attacking energy.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sutcliffe makes first Scotland start against Australia
content: Glasgow Warriors hooker Aicha Sutcliffe is set to make her first Scotland start in the WXV Global Series finale against Australia. Interim head coach Dave Butcher selected her as part of three changes for the match scheduled to take place in Canberra on Friday.
summary: Aicha Sutcliffe will make her first Scotland start in the final WXV Global Series match against Australia. Interim head coach Dave Butcher made three changes to the team for the game in Canberra.
author: BBC Sport

title: GB men finish fourth at Gymnastics World Championships, miss LA28 Olympic spot
content: Great Britain’s men’s gymnastics team finished fourth at the Gymnastics World Championships, narrowly missing an immediate qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. The team will now have to wait for an alternative pathway to secure their place at the LA28 Olympics.
summary: Great Britain placed fourth in the men's team final at the Gymnastics World Championships. The team just missed out on earning a spot at the 2028 Olympic Games on their first attempt.
author: BBC Sport

title: Man Utd Target Lewis Hall and Adrien Truffert in Transfer Move
content: Manchester United are reportedly targeting defenders Lewis Hall and Adrien Truffert, according to Wednesday's transfer gossip. Real Madrid remain interested in Riccardo Calafiori, while both Liverpool and Arsenal are keen on Xavi Espart.
summary: Manchester United are targeting Lewis Hall and Adrien Truffert according to Wednesday gossip. Real Madrid remain interested in Riccardo Calafiori, while Liverpool and Arsenal are keen on Xavi Espart.
author: BBC Sport

title: Arteta brushes off criticism as Raya responds to claims Arsenal play is boring
